CodePath Claude Corps Mentor Job 2026 – Remote Software Engineering Role with $110,000–$124,500 Salary

CodePath is expanding its team as artificial intelligence continues to reshape the global workforce, and qualified software engineers now have an opportunity to join its ambitious Claude Corps initiative as a Claude Corps Mentor. The position is designed for software engineers who have several years of professional engineering experience and a genuine interest in coaching, mentoring, reviewing code, and helping other engineers develop their technical capabilities through real-world production work. The role is 100% remote within the United States, offered on a full-time W-2 employee basis, and comes with an annual salary of $110,000 to $124,500, alongside a comprehensive employee benefits package. The successful candidate will work closely with fellows participating in Claude Corps, a national AI workforce initiative launched by CodePath and Anthropic. The mentor will provide technical coaching to approximately 20 fellows distributed across 8 to 12 host organizations, helping them improve their engineering practices, solve technical challenges, and successfully progress throughout the fellowship. Importantly, the position is not simply about writing software. It is designed for an engineer who can read other people’s code, identify problems, communicate constructive feedback, recognize recurring technical patterns, and help early-career engineers become stronger professionals.

About CodePath

CodePath is an organization focused on preparing the next generation of technical talent for careers in computer science and technology. According to the opportunity description, CodePath has trained more than 40,000 students from more than 1,000 universities and has worked with major technology companies, including Amazon and Google. The organization has spent nearly a decade developing technical talent and is now expanding its activities as artificial intelligence transforms the way organizations recruit, train, and employ technical professionals. CodePath’s broader vision is centered on using technical education and workforce development to convert talent into meaningful economic opportunity. The organization is also pursuing an ambitious AI workforce initiative with Anthropic, making this role particularly relevant for software engineers who want to participate in the development of AI-focused technical talent.

About the Claude Corps Initiative

In June 2026, CodePath and Anthropic launched Claude Corps, a national fellowship program supported by a $150 million commitment. The initiative aims to place 1,000 AI-trained fellows at nonprofit organizations across the United States. The program is designed to help fellows develop practical AI and software engineering capabilities while contributing to real organizational needs within nonprofit host organizations. The Claude Corps Mentor plays an important role in this model. Rather than being responsible for the fellows’ everyday organizational assignments, the mentor provides a technical coaching layer that follows the fellow throughout the program. This means the mentor may review code, provide feedback on technical decisions, identify development challenges, help fellows overcome roadblocks, and ensure that participants continue to develop as engineers.

About the Claude Corps Mentor Position

The Claude Corps Mentor is a full-time technical coaching position. The mentor will oversee a portfolio of approximately 10 pods, representing around 20 fellows across 8 to 12 host organizations. The position covers the fellows’ journey from the pre-Basecamp stage through the final day of the program.

The organizational structure is designed so that different people have different responsibilities:

  • The host organization directs the fellow’s day-to-day work.
  • The curriculum team is responsible for what fellows learn.
  • The Senior Manager of AI Practice is the manager of record and maintains the performance standard.
  • The Claude Corps Mentor provides continuous technical coaching and helps each fellow become better at their actual engineering work.

The mentor therefore acts as a technical throughline across the fellowship experience.

Key Details About the Job

  • Position: Claude Corps Mentor
  • Organization: CodePath
  • Location: Remote, United States
  • Employment type: Full-time W-2 employee
  • Reporting to: Senior Manager of AI Practice, Claude Corps
  • Annual salary: $110,000–$124,500
  • Expected start date: September 21, 2026
  • Cohort launch: October 19, 2026
  • Work arrangement: 100% remote within the United States

The provided opportunity description does not specify an application deadline. Applicants should therefore verify the current vacancy and application status before applying, particularly because the stated start date is September 21, 2026.

What Does a Claude Corps Mentor Do?

This position is intended for an engineer who enjoys developing other engineers. Instead of spending most of the working day building a product feature personally, the mentor helps approximately 20 fellows improve their ability to build software and solve technical problems. The work is predominantly written and asynchronous.

Typical activities include:

  • Reviewing pull requests.
  • Providing structured technical feedback.
  • Reviewing roadmap proposals.
  • Reviewing architecture proposals.
  • Giving feedback on quarterly business review deliverables.
  • Conducting weekly office hours.
  • Holding one-on-one meetings with fellows.
  • Participating in milestone reviews.
  • Supporting fellows when technical problems arise.
  • Identifying recurring technical patterns across multiple fellows.
  • Bringing in specialists when deeper technical expertise is required.
  • Helping fellows understand how to work effectively with AI-assisted development tools.

There will also be some synchronous work, including technical deep dives, cohort sessions, milestone reviews, and other meetings where real-time interaction is necessary.

Key Responsibilities

1. Coach Approximately 10 Pods

The mentor will manage a portfolio of approximately 10 pods containing about 20 fellows. Rather than concentrating on a single fellow or organization, the mentor will need to distribute their attention across the entire portfolio. This requires strong time management and the ability to identify which issues require immediate intervention and which can be handled asynchronously. The mentor will remain involved from pre-Basecamp through the final day of the program.

2. Review Fellows’ Technical Work

One of the most important responsibilities is reviewing the work fellows produce during the program. The mentor will have first access to fellows’ pull requests and provide structured written feedback.

This can include feedback on:

  • Code quality.
  • Architecture.
  • Technical decisions.
  • Development practices.
  • Roadmaps.
  • Engineering approaches.
  • Project deliverables.
  • Potential technical risks.

The objective is not merely to identify mistakes but to help fellows understand why a particular approach may be stronger and how they can improve their engineering judgment.

3. Conduct Weekly One-on-One Meetings

The mentor will facilitate weekly one-on-one meetings with fellows. These meetings provide an opportunity to understand:

  • Progress.
  • Challenges.
  • Technical difficulties.
  • Development goals.
  • Successes.
  • Areas requiring additional support.

The mentor is also expected to document fellow progress using the tools used by Claude Corps.

4. Lead Day 30, 90, 180 and 270 Reviews

The mentor will lead milestone reviews at several stages of the fellowship.

These include:

  • Day 30 review.
  • Day 90 review.
  • Day 180 review.
  • Day 270 review.

The mentor is responsible for synthesizing the fellow-level information and passing it to the Senior Manager of AI Practice. The senior manager then handles the broader roll-up and performance decision-making process.

5. Deliver Curriculum Within the Pods

Although the curriculum team develops the primary learning materials, mentors are responsible for delivering relevant modules within their pods. The mentor may also be asked to develop specialized content when a particular technical or learning gap becomes apparent. Because the mentor works closely with fellows, they may be among the first people to notice when a particular topic requires additional explanation or practical support.

6. Support Basecamp Assessments

The mentor will co-lead the Basecamp practical assessment alongside Anthropic instructors. This assessment provides an early opportunity to understand the technical abilities of each cohort and establish an initial calibration for the fellows.

7. Identify Program-Wide Technical Patterns

The mentor is expected to look beyond individual fellows and identify patterns that affect multiple participants. For example, if three or more fellows encounter a similar technical problem, the mentor should recognize the pattern and escalate it to the appropriate team. Depending on the nature of the issue, it may need to be directed to:

  • Claude Corps leadership.
  • The curriculum team.
  • Technical partner experts.
  • Host-organization managers.
  • The Senior Manager of AI Practice.

This makes the role both an individual coaching position and an important source of feedback for improving the overall program.

8. Help Fellows When Their Technical Work Is at Risk

The mentor will serve as one of the first points of contact when a fellow’s technical work encounters serious difficulties. The mentor should identify potential risks early, communicate them appropriately, and escalate issues to the Senior Manager of AI Practice when necessary. The goal is to prevent technical problems from becoming larger performance or program-delivery problems.

9. Work AI-Natively

AI-assisted software development is central to the role. The mentor is expected to have practical experience using AI development tools and should be capable of demonstrating effective AI-assisted engineering practices to the fellows.

Claude is specifically described as being part of the coaching workflow for activities such as:

  • Code review.
  • Pattern recognition.
  • Feedback.
  • Coaching at scale.

The mentor therefore needs to be comfortable working in an AI-enabled software engineering environment.

Key Success Metrics

Success in this role will be measured through concrete outcomes. The opportunity identifies several important indicators of success.

Identifying Technical Patterns

The mentor should identify the top three technical patterns emerging across the cohort and communicate those findings to the Senior Manager of AI Practice and curriculum team.

Demonstrating Impact With Host Organizations

Host-organization managers who have worked with the mentor during the previous 30 days should be able to provide at least one concrete example of the mentor’s impact. This emphasizes the importance of measurable coaching rather than simply completing meetings or reviewing documents.

Completing Day 30 Reviews

Every Day 30 review should be completed, documented, and delivered to the Senior Manager of AI Practice. For fellows whose work is at risk, the review should include a clear plan for intervention. For fellows who are progressing strongly, the mentor should identify appropriate opportunities for additional challenges and growth.

Required Qualifications

Applicants are expected to have a combination of professional software engineering experience, coaching ability, communication skills, and practical AI-assisted development experience.

Professional Software Engineering Experience

Candidates should have approximately 2 to 4 years of professional software engineering experience on a real team. The position is particularly suited to engineers who have progressed beyond entry-level work but are still close enough to the early-career experience to understand the challenges faced by junior engineers.

Coaching or Mentoring Experience

Formal management experience is not required.

Applicants can demonstrate coaching ability through a wide variety of experiences, including:

  • Mentoring interns.
  • Onboarding new teammates.
  • Teaching or assisting at a bootcamp.
  • Serving as a teaching assistant.
  • Helping junior engineers.
  • Informally coaching colleagues.
  • Participating in technical fellowship programs.

The emphasis is on demonstrating the instinct and ability to help other engineers improve.

Ability to Review Code

Candidates must be able to read and evaluate code they did not personally write. They should also be comfortable reviewing code written in technologies or stacks they do not use every day. More importantly, the candidate must be able to provide feedback that is specific, constructive, technically useful, and understandable to engineers with different technical backgrounds.

AI-Assisted Development Experience

Applicants must have experience shipping production software using AI-assisted development tools. Candidates should be able to explain specifically how AI has changed their engineering workflow. This requirement is particularly important because the fellows themselves are being trained to work in an AI-native environment.

Generalist Engineering Mindset

The mentor does not need to be the deepest expert in every technology used by every fellow. Instead, they need to be capable of finding answers quickly and identifying the appropriate expert when a problem requires deeper specialization. This makes adaptability, technical curiosity, and resourcefulness particularly important.

Strong Written Communication

Because much of the work is asynchronous, written communication is a critical requirement. Mentors will regularly communicate technical feedback to people who may use different programming languages, frameworks, or technology stacks. The ability to explain complex technical ideas clearly in writing is therefore essential.

Availability Across U.S. Time Zones

Applicants should be comfortable participating in remote synchronous activities across U.S. time zones. The position also requires approximately two evenings per month for cohort sessions and milestone reviews.

Preferred Qualifications

While not mandatory, several additional experiences may strengthen an application.

Preferred experience includes:

  • Teaching assistant experience.
  • Bootcamp coaching.
  • Fellowship mentoring.
  • Instructor experience.
  • Cohort-based training experience.
  • Experience working at a small or rapidly growing organization.
  • Experience translating business requirements into technical decisions.
  • Experience across multiple technical areas.

Candidates with experience in at least two of the following areas may be particularly well suited:

  • Web full-stack development.
  • Data engineering.
  • Artificial intelligence engineering.
  • Machine learning.
  • Infrastructure and DevOps.

Salary and Compensation

The Claude Corps Mentor position offers an annual salary ranging from:

$110,000 to $124,500 USD CodePath states that salaries are standardized according to the position’s level rather than being determined by the employee’s location within the United States. The role is classified as an Individual Contributor position. The final salary within the range depends on factors including the applicant’s relevant experience and skills as evaluated during the interview process.

Employee Benefits

In addition to the salary, the position provides a comprehensive benefits package.

Health and Wellness

Employees can receive:

  • Medical insurance.
  • Dental insurance.
  • Vision insurance.
  • 90% employer coverage for employees and dependents.
  • Employer-funded healthcare reimbursement.
  • Flexible Spending Accounts.
  • Employee Assistance Program.

Financial Security

The benefits package also includes:

  • 401(k) retirement plan.
  • Employer-paid life insurance.
  • Employer-paid disability insurance.
  • Identity theft protection.

Work-Life Balance

Employees receive several benefits designed to support personal and family well-being, including:

  • Generous paid time off.
  • Paid holidays.
  • 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave.
  • Annual year-end company closure from December 24 through January 2.

Professional Development

The position includes:

  • A $1,000 annual professional development stipend.
  • Home office setup support.

These benefits can be particularly valuable for a remote employee who wants to continue developing technical and professional skills.

Student Loan Forgiveness

CodePath states that it qualifies as an employer for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program.

This may provide an additional financial consideration for eligible employees managing qualifying student loan debt.

Additional Perks

Additional benefits listed in the opportunity include:

  • Pet wellness plans.
  • Legal services.
  • Home and auto insurance discounts.
  • Exclusive marketplace savings.

Why This Remote Software Engineering Role May Be Attractive

The position offers more than a conventional software engineering job.

For engineers interested in mentoring and workforce development, the role provides an opportunity to influence the growth of multiple engineers simultaneously.

Instead of measuring impact solely through features shipped or systems built, the mentor can measure impact through the development of other technical professionals.

The role may be particularly attractive to software engineers who:

  • Enjoy helping junior engineers grow.
  • Like reviewing and discussing technical work.
  • Prefer coaching over people management.
  • Have experience working with AI-assisted development.
  • Want to contribute to an emerging AI workforce initiative.
  • Enjoy remote work.
  • Want exposure to multiple organizations and engineering environments.
  • Prefer a generalist technical role.
  • Want to combine engineering experience with education and mentorship.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity may be a strong fit for a software engineer who has already gained several years of professional experience and has discovered an interest in helping other engineers succeed.

It is especially suited to someone who can look at a pull request and identify not only whether the code works, but also whether the engineer is developing good habits, making sound technical decisions, and learning from the experience.

The ideal candidate is not necessarily the person with the longest résumé or the deepest expertise in a single programming language.

Instead, the role emphasizes practical engineering judgment, coaching instincts, communication, adaptability, and the ability to work effectively with AI-assisted development tools.

Remote Work Arrangement

One of the major features of this position is that it is 100% remote.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the geographic requirement.

The vacancy specifies Remote, United States, and the benefits and employment arrangement are structured around U.S.-based employment.

Therefore, the position should not be interpreted as a worldwide remote job merely because the work can be performed remotely.

Applicants outside the United States should verify their eligibility with CodePath before investing time in the application process.

Important Start Date

The stated start date for the successful candidate is:

September 21, 2026

This date is scheduled ahead of the October 19, 2026 cohort launch.

Because the start date is relatively close, interested candidates should review the current vacancy and application instructions as soon as possible.

The supplied job description does not provide a specific application closing date.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants interested in the Claude Corps Mentor position should make sure their application clearly demonstrates the requirements most closely connected to the role.

Highlight Professional Engineering Experience

Clearly explain your professional software engineering experience.

Rather than simply listing programming languages, demonstrate the types of production systems, products, applications, or technical projects you have worked on.

Demonstrate Coaching Experience

Do not assume that mentoring experience only counts if you held an official mentor or manager title.

If you have:

  • Trained an intern.
  • Onboarded a colleague.
  • Served as a teaching assistant.
  • Helped junior engineers.
  • Led technical learning sessions.
  • Coached developers.
  • Supported a bootcamp.

make that experience visible in your application.

To apply click HERE

Explain Your AI Development Workflow

Because AI-assisted development is specifically required, applicants should be prepared to explain how AI tools have changed their engineering process. A strong application should go beyond saying that the candidate has “used AI.” It should demonstrate practical experience with AI-assisted engineering and explain how those tools have affected productivity, code review, debugging, development, documentation, testing, or other engineering activities.

Emphasize Written Communication

Since much of the coaching work occurs asynchronously, applicants should demonstrate an ability to communicate clearly in writing. Examples of technical documentation, architecture proposals, code review experience, developer documentation, or other written technical communication may help demonstrate this capability.

Show Evidence of Technical Breadth

Applicants should emphasize experience across multiple areas where relevant.

The preferred qualifications specifically mention combinations involving:

  • Full-stack web development.
  • Data and AI engineering.
  • Machine learning.
  • Infrastructure.
  • DevOps.

The role does not require mastery of every area, but evidence of technical breadth can strengthen an application.

For more information click here:

Key Takeaways for Applicants

Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully consider the following:

  1. The role is full-time, not a short-term freelance or contract position.
  2. The position is remote within the United States.
  3. The salary range is $110,000–$124,500 per year.
  4. The expected start date is September 21, 2026.
  5. The October 19, 2026 cohort launch is an important program milestone.
  6. Candidates should have 2–4 years of professional software engineering experience.
  7. Coaching or mentoring experience is required, but it does not have to come from a formal management position.
  8. Experience with AI-assisted software development tools is specifically required.
  9. Strong written communication is essential because much of the work is asynchronous.
  10. Applicants should be comfortable working across U.S. time zones.
  11. The role involves coaching approximately 20 fellows across 8–12 host organizations.
  12. The position includes a broad range of employee benefits in addition to the base salary.
  13. The supplied vacancy information does not state an application deadline, so applicants should check the live vacancy for current availability.

Conclusion

The CodePath Claude Corps Mentor position represents an opportunity for experienced early-career software engineers to combine technical expertise with coaching, mentorship, and AI workforce development. Through the Claude Corps initiative, CodePath and Anthropic are working to develop AI-trained technical talent and place fellows within nonprofit organizations across the United States. The mentor is a critical part of that model, providing the technical guidance and feedback fellows need while they work on real-world projects. With a salary of $110,000 to $124,500, full-time remote employment within the United States, professional development support, health and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, paid time off, and additional employee perks, the position offers a substantial package for qualified software engineers. The role is particularly suited to candidates who have several years of professional engineering experience, enjoy mentoring others, can confidently review production code, communicate technical feedback clearly, and have practical experience using AI-assisted development tools. For software engineers who want to move beyond simply building software and instead help develop the engineers who will build the next generation of AI-enabled technology, this Claude Corps Mentor opportunity could provide a distinctive path to make that impact. Interested candidates should carefully review the current CodePath vacancy, confirm the latest application instructions and eligibility requirements, and prepare an application that clearly demonstrates both their engineering experience and their ability to coach other technical professionals

item.content:encoded:
The Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies (OCIS) Fellowship 2027 is offering an exceptional opportunity for experienced professionals and academics to undertake independent research at the prestigious Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies in the United Kingdom.

The fellowship is a collaboration between the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies (OCIS). It is designed for established professionals and academics whose work contributes to a deeper and more informed understanding of Islamic culture and civilisation, contemporary Muslim societies, international relations, diplomacy, interfaith dialogue, leadership and public policy.

The programme provides selected fellows with the opportunity to spend five months at OCIS, from October 2027 to March 2028, developing a self-directed research project while accessing academic resources, intellectual networks and opportunities for intercultural exchange.

A total of six exceptional candidates will be selected for the fellowship.

Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies Fellowship 2027 at a Glance

  • Programme: Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies (OCIS) Fellowship
  • Host institution: Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies, University of Oxford
  • Programme partners: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies
  • Location: Oxford, United Kingdom
  • Duration: Five months
  • Expected period: October 2027 to March 2028
  • Number of fellows: Six
  • Application deadline: 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC
  • Research format: Self-directed research
  • Funding: Living expenses, return economy airfare and research-related allowances
  • Target applicants: Mid-career professionals and academics
  • Application: Through the official Chevening application system

What Is the Chevening OCIS Fellowship?

The Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies Fellowship is a specialised international fellowship intended to bring experienced academics and professionals to Oxford for an intensive period of independent research and intellectual engagement.

Unlike a conventional taught degree programme, the fellowship is centred on the fellow’s own research project. Applicants are expected to identify a research area relevant to the objectives of the fellowship and develop a clear proposal explaining the central research question and how they intend to undertake the research during their residence at OCIS.

The programme provides an opportunity to examine issues connected to Islamic thought, Muslim societies, diplomacy, international relations, policy and intercultural understanding from a range of academic and professional perspectives.

The fellowship can therefore be particularly valuable for individuals whose work sits at the intersection of academia, policy, diplomacy, international development, economics, public affairs, social sciences, culture, religion, science and technology or other fields connected to the Muslim world.

What Does the Fellowship Focus On?

The programme encourages research and academic activities that contribute to a more informed understanding of the culture and civilisation of Islam and contemporary Muslim societies.

Fellows can explore a broad range of subjects, including:

  • Islamic culture and civilisation
  • Islamic history
  • Classical Islamic sciences
  • Contemporary Muslim societies
  • Islamic thought
  • Economics and Islamic finance
  • Public health in the Muslim world
  • Science and technology in Muslim societies
  • Muslims and Muslim communities in Western societies
  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • Interfaith dialogue
  • Inter-civilisational relations
  • Public policy
  • Leadership in diverse cultural environments

This breadth means that prospective applicants should not necessarily interpret the fellowship as being limited to religious studies. Instead, it provides an interdisciplinary environment in which questions concerning Muslim societies and the relationship between the Islamic world and the wider international community can be examined through academic, policy and professional perspectives.

A Unique Opportunity for Independent Research

One of the most distinctive features of the Chevening OCIS Fellowship is its emphasis on self-directed research.

Successful applicants are expected to arrive at OCIS with a defined research idea rather than simply participating in a predetermined curriculum.

When applying, candidates should therefore be prepared to present a short research proposal covering:

  1. The research topic they intend to investigate.
  2. The main research question guiding the project.
  3. The significance of the research and why the topic deserves further examination.
  4. The proposed approach or methodology they intend to use.
  5. How the research will be conducted during their residence at OCIS.

A strong proposal should demonstrate that the applicant has thought carefully about the subject, understands the broader context and has a realistic plan for completing meaningful research within the five-month fellowship period.

What Will Fellows Gain From the Programme?

The fellowship is designed to provide both intellectual and professional benefits.

1. Five Months of Research at OCIS

Selected fellows will spend five months undertaking research at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies.

This provides dedicated time away from many of the competing demands of a normal professional or academic position, allowing fellows to concentrate on developing their research project.

2. Access to Academic Resources

Fellows will benefit from access to world-class academic resources and an intellectually stimulating research environment.

Being based in Oxford can also provide opportunities to engage with a wider academic community and participate in intellectual activities taking place across the university environment.

3. Academic and Professional Mentorship

The programme provides opportunities for fellows to interact with experienced academics and other professionals.

Such interactions can help fellows refine their research ideas, strengthen their analytical approaches and gain perspectives that can contribute to their professional and academic development.

4. Intercultural and Inter-Civilisational Dialogue

The fellowship encourages dialogue across cultural and intellectual traditions.

Fellows can engage with questions concerning relationships between Muslim societies and the wider international community while developing a deeper understanding of different cultural and historical perspectives.

5. Leadership Development

The experience can contribute to enhanced leadership capabilities by exposing fellows to complex global issues and encouraging critical engagement with questions of policy, diplomacy, society and international cooperation.

6. Policy Insight

For professionals working in government, diplomacy, international development, research, academia, communications or policy-related fields, the fellowship can provide an opportunity to explore how research and intellectual analysis can contribute to better policy understanding and decision-making.

Fellowship Duration

The Chevening OCIS Fellowship lasts for five months.

The programme is scheduled to run:

  • Start: October
  • End: March

During this period, fellows will be based at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies and focus on their approved research projects.

Financial Support and Fellowship Benefits

The Chevening OCIS Fellowship provides substantial financial support to successful fellows.

Each fellowship includes:

  • A five-month research period at OCIS
  • Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship
  • Return economy-class airfare to the United Kingdom
  • An allowance package for research-related activities

This funding structure is intended to enable selected fellows to concentrate on their research and professional development while residing in Oxford.

Applicants should, however, carefully review the official fellowship terms and conditions for the complete details of the financial package and any applicable provisions.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The Chevening OCIS Fellowship is specifically intended for mid-career professionals and academics.

Applicants must meet the standard Chevening fellowship eligibility requirements in addition to the programme-specific requirements.

For this particular fellowship, candidates must:

  • Be citizens of an eligible country listed by the programme.
  • Be resident in one of the eligible countries at the time of application.
  • Hold a postgraduate-level qualification, or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant area.
  • Have significant professional and/or academic research experience.
  • Have at least five years of relevant professional and/or academic research experience.

The fellowship is therefore aimed at experienced candidates rather than recent graduates with limited professional or research experience.

Eligible Countries

Applicants must be citizens of, and resident in, one of the following countries at the time of application:

  1. Afghanistan
  2. Algeria
  3. Azerbaijan
  4. Bangladesh
  5. Egypt
  6. Indonesia
  7. Iraq
  8. Jordan
  9. Kazakhstan
  10. Kyrgyzstan
  11. Lebanon
  12. Libya
  13. Malaysia
  14. Morocco
  15. Nigeria
  16. Pakistan
  17. Palestine
  18. Philippines
  19. Senegal
  20. Sudan
  21. Syria
  22. Tajikistan
  23. Tunisia
  24. Turkey
  25. Turkmenistan
  26. Uzbekistan

Applicants should confirm their eligibility against the official Chevening requirements before beginning an application, as programme requirements and country eligibility can be subject to change.

Important Visa Information for Applicants From Afghanistan and Sudan

The programme specifically highlights an important distinction concerning applicants from Afghanistan and Sudan.

According to the fellowship information, recent UK Government legislation affects the ability of citizens of these countries to obtain a Study Visa to enter the United Kingdom.

However, this does not prevent Afghan and Sudanese citizens from applying for the Chevening OCIS Fellowship because fellowship visa routes are treated differently.

The programme states that citizens of Afghanistan and Sudan remain eligible to apply for the Chevening OCIS Fellowship.

Applicants from these countries should nevertheless consult the latest information published by the UK Government regarding applicable visa requirements before making travel arrangements.

What Kind of Candidates Is Chevening Looking For?

The fellowship is particularly suited to professionals and academics who can demonstrate a strong connection between their experience, research interests and the programme’s objectives.

Potential applicants may include experienced individuals working in areas such as:

  • Academia and higher education
  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • Government and public policy
  • International development
  • Economics
  • Islamic finance
  • Public health
  • Science and technology
  • Social sciences
  • History and civilisation
  • Cultural studies
  • Interfaith relations
  • International cooperation
  • Research and policy analysis
  • Communications and public affairs
  • Leadership and governance

The important consideration is not simply the applicant’s job title. Candidates should be able to demonstrate meaningful professional or academic experience and a credible research interest that aligns with the purpose of the fellowship.

The Research Proposal Is an Important Part of the Application

Prospective applicants should give particular attention to the research proposal.

The proposal provides the selection panel with an opportunity to understand what the applicant intends to accomplish during the five-month period at OCIS.

A well-developed proposal should clearly communicate:

The problem or issue

Explain what issue the research will examine and why it is important.

The research question

Identify a focused and researchable question rather than presenting an overly broad subject.

The relevance

Explain how the proposed research contributes to a better understanding of Islamic culture, civilisation, contemporary Muslim societies or related issues within the fellowship’s scope.

The methodology

Describe how the research will be conducted during the fellowship.

The expected contribution

Explain what the research could contribute to academic discussion, policy debates, professional practice or broader understanding.

Applicants should ensure that the proposed project is realistic for a five-month period.

How Does the Selection Process Work?

The Chevening OCIS Fellowship selection process consists of two interview stages.

First Interview: British Embassies and High Commissions

The first interview is conducted with representatives from British embassies and high commissions.

Candidates should be prepared to discuss:

  • Their suitability for the fellowship
  • Their professional and academic background
  • Their motivation for applying
  • Their research interests
  • Their understanding of the fellowship
  • Why the proposed research matters
  • How the fellowship fits into their professional or academic objectives

Candidates should be able to explain clearly why they are an appropriate candidate and what they hope to achieve through the opportunity.

Second Interview: Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies

Successful candidates from the first stage will be invited to a second and final interview with representatives from OCIS.

This interview will focus more deeply on the applicant’s research interests.

Applicants should therefore expect detailed questions about their proposed research project, including the subject, research question, methodology, relevance and intended outcomes.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Applicants interested in the Chevening OCIS Fellowship should begin preparing well before the deadline.

1. Establish Your Research Focus

Identify a research question that is specific, meaningful and aligned with the fellowship.

Avoid choosing a topic simply because it sounds broad or prestigious. The strongest projects are likely to demonstrate a clear intellectual purpose.

2. Connect Your Experience to the Research

Your professional and academic background should provide a convincing foundation for the proposed project.

Explain how your previous experience has led you to the research question you want to investigate.

3. Demonstrate Mid-Career Experience

Because the fellowship requires significant professional and/or academic research experience, applicants should clearly demonstrate the depth and relevance of their experience.

4. Explain Why Oxford and OCIS Matter

Applicants should be able to articulate why undertaking the research at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies would be particularly valuable.

Consider the academic environment, resources, intellectual exchange, research opportunities and relevance of the centre to your project.

5. Prepare for Both Interviews

Do not treat the application as the final stage.

Successful applicants will need to explain their research and motivations during two interview stages, with the second interview placing particular emphasis on the research interests.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies Fellowship 2027 is:

6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. Preparing a strong research proposal, gathering the required information and reviewing eligibility requirements can take considerable time.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit their applications through the official Chevening application platform.

Official application portal:
Apply for the Chevening OCIS Fellowship

Applicants should also review the official Chevening fellowship eligibility requirements before submitting their application.

Chevening Fellowship Eligibility Requirements

For additional information and frequently asked questions, applicants can consult the official Chevening resources.

Chevening Fellowships

APPLY HERE

Why This Fellowship Is Valuable for Mid-Career Professionals and Academics

The Chevening OCIS Fellowship stands out because it combines research, international exposure, leadership development, intercultural dialogue and policy engagement within an internationally recognised academic environment.

For a professional who has spent several years developing expertise in a particular field, five months dedicated to research can provide an opportunity to step back from routine responsibilities and explore a question in considerably greater depth.

For academics, the programme can provide an environment in which an existing research agenda can be developed further while engaging with a wider international intellectual community.

For professionals working in diplomacy, government, international relations, development or policy, the fellowship can also provide an opportunity to examine global challenges through perspectives informed by Islamic thought and the experiences of Muslim societies.

What Makes the Fellowship Different?

Several characteristics distinguish the Chevening OCIS Fellowship from many other international opportunities.

It is research-focused

The programme is centred on a research project developed by the fellow rather than a conventional taught course.

It is designed for experienced professionals

The requirement for at least five years of significant professional and/or academic research experience makes this a mid-career opportunity.

It is interdisciplinary

The areas of interest span history, economics, finance, public health, science, technology, international relations, diplomacy and other fields.

It encourages intercultural understanding

The programme promotes dialogue and deeper understanding between Islamic societies and the wider international community.

It is hosted in Oxford

Fellows undertake their research at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies, providing access to an internationally recognised academic environment.

Visit HERE for more information about the Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies Fellowship 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Chevening OCIS Fellowship a scholarship?

No. It is a fellowship designed for mid-career professionals and academics undertaking self-directed research.

How long is the fellowship?

The fellowship lasts five months, from October to March.

How many fellows will be selected?

The programme will select six exceptional candidates.

Is the fellowship fully funded?

The fellowship includes living expenses, return economy airfare and an allowance package for research-related activities.

Do applicants need a postgraduate qualification?

Yes. Applicants must hold a postgraduate-level qualification or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant area at the time of application.

Is professional experience required?

Yes. Applicants must have significant professional and/or academic research experience, with at least five years required.

Can applicants from Africa apply?

Yes, but only citizens of countries specifically included in the eligible-country list can apply. Eligible African countries listed for this fellowship include Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal and Sudan.

Can applicants from Kenya apply?

Kenya is not included in the eligible-country list provided for the Chevening OCIS Fellowship. Therefore, Kenyan citizens should not assume that they qualify for this particular fellowship based on eligibility for other Chevening programmes.

Can Afghan and Sudanese citizens apply?

Yes. The programme explicitly states that citizens of Afghanistan and Sudan remain eligible to apply, although they should carefully review current UK visa guidance.

Is the research topic predetermined?

No. Fellows undertake self-directed research based on their own approved project.

Will there be an interview?

Yes. The selection process involves two interview stages. The first is with British embassies or high commissions, while the final interview is with representatives from OCIS.

Conclusion

The Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies Fellowship 2027 offers an important opportunity for experienced academics and professionals seeking to deepen their research, broaden their international perspectives and contribute to greater understanding of Islamic culture, civilisation and contemporary Muslim societies.

With five months of research at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies, financial support covering living expenses and return economy airfare, access to academic resources and opportunities for intellectual and intercultural exchange, the fellowship can provide significant value to candidates with a well-developed research agenda.

However, this is a highly specialised opportunity. Applicants should carefully assess their eligibility, particularly the country and residency requirements, postgraduate-level qualification requirement and minimum five years of professional and/or academic research experience.

The research proposal should also be treated as a central component of the application. Candidates should develop a focused research question, demonstrate why the topic matters and explain how they will realistically undertake the project during their five-month residence.

Eligible mid-career professionals and academics who have a strong research interest aligned with the programme should therefore begin preparing early and submit their applications before the 6 October 2026 deadline at 11:00 UTC.

For official information and application instructions, applicants should rely on the Chevening official website and the official application portal.

Applications are open for the Killam Fellowships Program 2027–2028, a prestigious undergraduate exchange opportunity that enables outstanding Canadian and American students to study in the neighbouring country for one semester or a complete academic year.

Canadian undergraduate students can use the program to study at a university in the United States, while eligible American students can study at a Canadian institution. Successful applicants receive US$6,000 for one semester or US$12,000 for a full academic year, together with a health benefit plan and access to academic, cultural and professional enrichment activities.

The 2027–2028 competition officially opened on 15 August 2026. The open-competition deadline is 31 January 2027. Students applying through a direct exchange must follow the internal deadline established by their home institution, which may be considerably earlier.

Killam Fellowships 2027–2028 at a Glance

Program detail Information
Program name Killam Fellowships Program
Administered by Fulbright Canada
Exchange direction Canada to the United States or the United States to Canada
Academic level Undergraduate
Exchange duration One semester or one full academic year
Award for one semester US$6,000
Award for a full academic year US$12,000
Additional support Health benefit plan and enrichment programming
Mobility funding Up to US$800 for Canadian Fellows or CAD$800 for American Fellows
Competition opening date 15 August 2026
Open-competition deadline 31 January 2027
Direct-exchange deadline Varies according to each participating home institution
Placement period Fall 2027, Spring 2028 or the full 2027–2028 academic year
Eligible nationalities Canadian and United States citizens

What Is the Killam Fellowships Program?

The Killam Fellowships Program is a reciprocal undergraduate exchange initiative administered by Fulbright Canada. It gives academically accomplished students from Canada and the United States an opportunity to live and study in the other country.

The program is intended to deepen academic cooperation, intercultural understanding and long-term relationships between Canada and the United States. Students do more than complete courses at a host institution. They also participate in structured orientation, cultural activities, educational travel and cross-border programming.

Participants may complete:

  • One academic semester in the host country; or
  • A full academic year in the host country.

Canadian recipients attend an institution in the United States, while American recipients attend an institution in Canada.

Two Application Routes

Students may participate through either the direct exchange route or the open competition. Applicants should understand the financial and administrative differences before selecting a route.

1. Direct Exchange Program

Under the direct exchange arrangement, students:

  • Remain registered at their home university.
  • Pay the regular tuition and other required fees to their home institution.
  • Attend the host institution as an exchange student.
  • Must be enrolled at a participating Killam partner institution.
  • Must select a participating institution in the other country.
  • Must obtain nomination from their home university.
  • Must meet their university’s internal application deadline.

Participating universities may nominate up to three full-year candidates or six one-semester candidates. Nomination does not automatically guarantee selection because the applications are subsequently reviewed through the program’s independent adjudication process.

This route may be financially preferable where the student’s home tuition is lower than the tuition charged by the proposed host university. Students should nevertheless verify how scholarships, financial aid, residence costs and mandatory institutional fees will be treated during the exchange.

2. Open Competition

The open competition allows eligible students to apply even if their home university is not a Killam direct-exchange partner.

Under this route, students:

  • May be enrolled at any eligible degree-granting institution in Canada or the United States.
  • Apply independently to an eligible degree-granting host institution in the other country.
  • Register at the host institution as a visiting or self-placed student.
  • Pay tuition and required fees directly to the host institution.
  • Must secure admission or acceptance from the proposed host institution.
  • Submit the fellowship application directly by 31 January 2027.

Open-competition applicants should not assume that the fellowship award will cover the complete cost of host tuition, accommodation, travel and living expenses. The US$6,000-per-semester award is substantial support, but applicants must prepare a realistic financial plan based on the actual costs of the selected host university and city.

Detailed guidance for each route is available on the official Canadian application page and American application page.

Financial Benefits

Cash Award

Each selected participant receives:

  • US$6,000 for a one-semester exchange; or
  • US$12,000 for a full academic-year exchange.

The award is intended to support the costs associated with studying and living in the host country. Applicants should independently calculate whether additional personal, institutional or family funding will be required.

Health Benefit Plan

Fulbright Canada provides Killam Fellows with a health benefit plan during the award period. Students should carefully review the coverage terms after selection and determine whether supplementary insurance is required for conditions, activities or expenses not covered by the program plan.

Mobility Grant

Killam Fellows may apply competitively for an additional mobility grant to undertake educational or cultural travel within the host country.

The maximum mobility funding is:

  • Up to US$800 for Canadian students studying in the United States.
  • Up to CAD$800 for American students studying in Canada.

The proposed activity should take place away from the student’s host-university location and contribute to a broader understanding of the host country. It does not necessarily have to be directly connected to the student’s academic specialization, but it should have a clear educational or cultural purpose.

Mobility funding is competitive and should not be treated as an automatic component of every award.

Fall Orientation in Ottawa

New Killam Fellows participate in a three-day orientation program in Ottawa, Ontario. The orientation helps students understand their responsibilities, prepare for the exchange experience and develop relationships with other Canadian and American Fellows.

The program also provides an opportunity to learn about Canada–United States relations, cross-border cooperation and the objectives of Fulbright Canada.

Spring Seminar in Washington, D.C.

Killam Fellows also participate in a three-day spring seminar in Washington, D.C. The seminar generally takes place in April and combines academic, cultural and public-policy activities.

Participants may engage with representatives from government, diplomatic, academic and policy institutions while learning about the relationship between Canada and the United States. Fulbright Canada states that it covers reasonable costs associated with the official spring seminar.

Opportunities After the Exchange

Participation can continue to create opportunities after the exchange period. Killam Fellows and alumni may become eligible for initiatives such as:

  • Community-action funding for volunteer-led projects.
  • Fulbright Canada alumni internship opportunities.
  • Alumni mentoring and networking.
  • The Local Ambassador Program.
  • Community and cultural enrichment activities.
  • Continued engagement with the wider Fulbright Canada network.

Availability, funding amounts and application conditions for alumni opportunities may change from one competition cycle to another.

Eligibility Requirements for Canadian Applicants

According to the current eligibility requirements for Canadian students, applicants must:

  • Be Canadian citizens.
  • Be enrolled full-time as undergraduate students.
  • Be in good academic standing at a degree-granting institution in Canada.
  • Expect to receive their undergraduate degree in spring 2028 or later.
  • Meet the international-exchange and academic requirements of their home university.
  • Have proficiency in English or French, where appropriate.
  • Possess a strong and competitive academic record.
  • complete the application process before the applicable deadline.
  • Obtain nomination from their home institution when applying through the direct exchange.

Canadian students selected for the program will undertake their exchange in the United States.

Eligibility Requirements for American Applicants

According to the current eligibility requirements for American students, applicants must:

  • Be citizens of the United States.
  • Be enrolled full-time as undergraduate students.
  • Be in good academic standing at a fully accredited, degree-granting college or university in the United States.
  • Expect to receive their undergraduate degree in spring 2028 or later.
  • Meet the international-exchange requirements of their home institution.
  • Have proficiency in English or French, where appropriate.
  • Have a superior and competitive academic record.
  • Complete all parts of the application before the applicable deadline.
  • Obtain nomination from their university when applying through the direct exchange.

American recipients complete their exchange at a Canadian institution.

Academic Fields and Degree Restrictions

The formal eligibility pages do not identify a narrow list of approved academic disciplines. Students from different undergraduate fields may therefore be considered, subject to course availability and host-university approval.

However, Fulbright Canada’s application guidance identifies BA, BSc and BAH students as the standard applicant group and states that professional degrees are normally not eligible. Students enrolled in medicine, dentistry, law or another professional program should obtain confirmation from Fulbright Canada and their home university before preparing an application.

Applicants must also ensure that their proposed host courses:

  • Are available during the intended exchange semester.
  • Can be approved by their home university.
  • Will support progress toward their undergraduate degree.
  • Meet any prerequisites imposed by the host institution.
  • Are taught in a language in which the applicant can participate effectively.

Participating American Universities

Students applying through the direct exchange should check the current institutional fact sheets because exchange spaces, academic restrictions and course availability may vary.

Participating American institutions listed by Fulbright Canada include:

  1. American University
  2. Arizona State University
  3. Bridgewater State University
  4. Clemson University
  5. Florida Polytechnic University
  6. Georgia Institute of Technology
  7. Ithaca College
  8. Miami Dade College
  9. Ohio University
  10. Smith College
  11. State University of New York College at Plattsburgh
  12. University of California, Irvine
  13. University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
  14. University of Maine
  15. University of South Alabama
  16. University of Texas at Austin
  17. University of Virginia
  18. University of Washington
  19. Wellesley College

Participating Canadian Universities

Participating Canadian institutions listed by Fulbright Canada include:

  1. Acadia University
  2. Brock University
  3. Carleton University
  4. Dalhousie University
  5. McGill University
  6. McMaster University
  7. Memorial University of Newfoundland
  8. Mount Allison University
  9. Queen’s University
  10. Saint Mary’s University
  11. Université de Montréal
  12. Université Laval
  13. University of Alberta
  14. University of Calgary
  15. University of Ottawa
  16. University of Prince Edward Island
  17. University of Toronto
  18. University of Victoria
  19. Western University
  20. York University

The open competition is not limited to this partner list. Eligible open-competition applicants may apply to other degree-granting institutions in the host country, subject to admission, program approval and the competition rules.

Required Application Documents

Applicants should prepare the following materials:

1. Proof of Citizenship

A one-page PDF showing Canadian or United States citizenship is required. A passport is the preferred document.

2. Curriculum Vitae

The CV must:

  • Be submitted as a PDF.
  • Be no longer than three pages.
  • Use 12-point font.
  • Use margins of approximately one inch or 2.54 centimetres.

The CV should present the applicant’s academic background, employment, leadership, volunteering, extracurricular involvement, honours, awards and relevant international or community experience.

3. Academic Transcripts

Applicants must submit unofficial transcripts from every post-secondary institution they have attended.

The academic adviser may also be required to calculate the applicant’s cumulative grade-point average on a 4.0 scale.

4. Personal Statement

Applicants must provide a one-page, single-spaced personal statement using 12-point font and one-inch margins.

The statement should explain:

  • Why the applicant wants to study in the neighbouring country.
  • How the proposed exchange supports their academic goals.
  • Why the selected host institution and courses are appropriate.
  • How the experience will support personal and professional development.
  • What the applicant can contribute to the Killam community.
  • How the applicant may promote stronger cross-border understanding.

5. Supplementary Document Package

The supplementary package includes a cover form that must be completed by the student’s adviser.

6. Course Selection Forms

Applicants must prepare course-selection documentation for their proposed host institutions. The relevant forms must be reviewed and signed by an authorized official at the home university.

Direct-exchange applicants generally provide forms for their top three institutional choices. Open-competition applicants should follow the instructions applicable to each proposed institution.

7. Host-University Acceptance Letters

Open-competition applicants should include admission or acceptance letters if they have already received them. The final award remains subject to acceptance by the host institution.

8. Two References

Applicants must enter requests for two references through the application system. Referees should be able to evaluate the applicant’s academic performance, character, leadership potential, maturity and ability to benefit from an international exchange.

How Applications Are Evaluated

Applications are reviewed and ranked by an independent adjudication committee consisting of faculty representatives from participating universities and senior officials from Fulbright Canada.

The assessment considers:

  • The quality and feasibility of the proposed academic program.
  • The applicant’s personal statement.
  • Academic achievement and overall academic record.
  • Letters of reference.
  • The applicant’s preparation for cross-cultural study.
  • Alignment between the exchange plan and the applicant’s academic goals.

The committee produces a list of recommended candidates and alternates. Final awards remain subject to:

  • Availability of program funding.
  • Acceptance by the proposed host institution.
  • Approval from the relevant home university.
  • The applicant’s ability to obtain the required immigration documentation.
  • Compliance with the current entry and visa requirements of the host country.

Application Deadlines

Open Competition

The application deadline for the 2027–2028 open competition is:

31 January 2027

This deadline applies to eligible Canadian and American applicants using the self-placed or open-competition route.

Direct Exchange

There is no single universal deadline for direct-exchange applicants.

Every participating home institution establishes its own internal competition deadline. These institutional deadlines may occur weeks or months before 31 January 2027.

Students interested in the direct exchange should immediately contact:

  • Their study-abroad office.
  • International programs office.
  • Exchange coordinator.
  • Academic adviser.
  • The institutional representative responsible for Killam nominations.

Missing the internal university deadline will normally prevent a direct-exchange applicant from being nominated.

Application Links

Canadian students can review the official instructions and begin their application through the Canadian Killam Fellowships application page.

American students can review the official instructions and begin their application through the American Killam Fellowships application page.

Applicants should also consult the main Killam Fellowships Program page for program updates and partner information.

Important Application Advice

  1. Contact your university first

Determine whether your institution participates in the direct exchange and confirm its internal deadline before beginning the application.

  1. Compare the financial consequences of both routes

Direct-exchange students pay home-university fees, while open-competition students pay the host institution. This distinction can substantially affect the total cost of participation.

  1. Obtain course approval early

Do not assume that selected host courses will automatically transfer toward your degree. Seek written academic approval wherever possible.

  1. Select references strategically

Choose referees who can provide detailed evidence of academic ability, maturity, leadership and readiness for an international experience.

  1. Develop a specific personal statement

A competitive statement should connect the selected institution, proposed courses, academic objectives and broader interest in Canada–United States relations.

  1. Prepare for additional expenses

The award should not automatically be treated as complete funding. Budget for tuition, housing, food, visas, immigration documents, flights, local transport, books and personal expenses.

  1. Review visa and immigration requirements

Awards are conditional upon the student’s ability to obtain the appropriate permission to study in the host country.

  1. Submit carefully

Complete all application fields in English, upload only the requested documents and review the application before submission. The online system may not allow changes after the final submission.

Conclusion

The Killam Fellowships Program 2027–2028 offers academically strong Canadian and American undergraduate students a valuable opportunity to study in the neighbouring country while receiving significant financial and institutional support.

With an award of US$6,000 per semester or US$12,000 for a full academic year, a health benefit plan, cultural programming in Ottawa and Washington, and access to additional mobility and alumni opportunities, the program provides far more than an ordinary university exchange.

Applicants must select the correct application route, confirm their eligibility, obtain academic approval for their proposed courses and prepare a strong application supported by credible references. Open-competition applications close on 31 January 2027, while direct-exchange candidates must comply with the earlier internal deadline set by their home university.
