item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the PMNCH Advocating for Change for Adolescents Initiative AY Grants 2026–2027, offering national youth-led and youth-serving organizations, coalitions, and networks an opportunity to receive up to US$15,000 in grant funding to advance adolescent health and well-being and sexual and reproductive health and rights at the national level.

The Partnership for Maternal, Newborn & Child Health (PMNCH) is inviting eligible organizations to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for catalytic funding under its Advocating for Change for Adolescents initiative.

The new funding phase will run for 12 months, from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027, and is intended to strengthen youth-led advocacy, improve national coordination, build the capacities of adolescent and youth advocates, increase the visibility of adolescent health priorities, and strengthen accountability for government commitments.

Organizations interested in the funding opportunity must act quickly. The application deadline is 12:00 CEST on 21 August 2026.

About the Advocating for Change for Adolescents Initiative

The Advocating for Change for Adolescents initiative is an established PMNCH programme focused on strengthening the ability of young people and youth organizations to influence policies, commitments, and actions affecting adolescent health and well-being.

The programme has been supporting youth-led advocacy since 2017, particularly in the areas of adolescent health and well-being (AHWB) and sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR).

Through previous phases of the AY Grants programme between 2017 and 2025, the initiative has worked to develop a stronger community of empowered young advocates while supporting efforts to improve national accountability for commitments made by governments.

The 2026–2027 funding round represents the next phase of this work.

Rather than supporting isolated advocacy activities, this phase seeks to strengthen national-level implementation and collaboration. Successful organizations will be expected to contribute to country priorities and, where applicable, work alongside existing national Collaborative Advocacy Action Plan (CAAP) structures instead of establishing parallel or duplicative initiatives.

The programme is also aligned with the PMNCH Strategy 2026–2030 and builds on achievements and lessons from earlier AY Grants phases.

What Will the PMNCH AY Grants 2026–2027 Support?

The next phase of the grants will support implementation of PMNCH adolescent health and well-being activities at the national level.

Funding is intended to help organizations undertake advocacy and related activities that contribute to stronger adolescent health and well-being outcomes, including issues connected with sexual and reproductive health and rights.

The grants are expected to support organizations in several interconnected areas.

1. Strengthening National Coordination and Collaboration

One of the major objectives is to improve coordination between partners working to advance adolescent health and well-being priorities within participating countries.

Organizations should not approach this work in isolation.

Where Collaborative Advocacy Action Plan initiatives already operate nationally, funded organizations will be expected to work jointly with the relevant structures rather than establish parallel initiatives that could duplicate existing efforts.

This approach is intended to strengthen collective advocacy and encourage organizations working toward similar adolescent health objectives to coordinate their activities and priorities.

2. Building the Capacity of Adolescents and Young People

The initiative seeks to increase awareness among adolescents and young people while strengthening their capacity to participate meaningfully in advocacy.

A major goal is to build a cadre of empowered adolescent and youth advocates who possess the knowledge and skills required to champion adolescent health and well-being priorities.

This includes advocacy relating to sexual and reproductive health and rights.

Capacity development is therefore an important part of the programme. Organizations should consider how their activities can equip adolescents and young people with practical advocacy capabilities rather than limiting youth participation to consultation alone.

3. Strengthening Accountability for Government Commitments

The grants will also support efforts to enhance accountability for national government commitments concerning adolescent health and well-being.

Successful organizations may therefore contribute to monitoring, advocacy, engagement, and follow-up activities designed to ensure that relevant national commitments translate into meaningful action.

The initiative recognizes that commitments alone are insufficient without mechanisms that encourage implementation, transparency, follow-up, and accountability.

4. Increasing the Visibility of Adolescent Health and Well-Being

Another important objective is to raise the visibility of adolescent health and well-being issues among influential national stakeholders.

These stakeholders may include:

  • National governments and relevant public institutions;
  • Civil society organizations;
  • United Nations agencies;
  • Philanthropic organizations;
  • Youth organizations and networks;
  • Advocacy coalitions; and
  • Other actors capable of influencing adolescent health policies, financing, programmes, and accountability.

Through increased visibility and coordinated advocacy, the initiative aims to keep adolescent health and well-being priorities prominent within national policy and development discussions.

Countries Eligible for the AY Grants 2026–2027

The funding opportunity is available to eligible national organizations, coalitions, and networks operating in a defined group of countries.

The participating countries are divided between those currently identified as CAAP-focused countries and additional non-CAAP-focused countries.

CAAP-Focused Countries

Eligible organizations may apply from:

  • Liberia
  • Malawi
  • Nigeria
  • Senegal
  • Sierra Leone
  • South Africa
  • Tanzania
  • Zambia

Non-CAAP-Focused Countries

Applications are also being accepted from:

  • India
  • Colombia

Organizations should be based in the country for which they are submitting an application and should meet the formal recognition or registration requirements described in the eligibility criteria.

Eligibility Requirements for PMNCH AY Grants 2026–2027

PMNCH has established several requirements that organizations should meet to be considered for funding.

Youth Leadership or Strong Youth Engagement

Applicant organizations should be youth-led, with young people approximately 15 to 29 years old holding meaningful leadership or governance positions.

This requirement emphasizes substantive youth leadership rather than participation in name only.

However, the opportunity is not restricted exclusively to organizations formally categorized as youth-led. A youth-serving organization may also qualify when it can demonstrate a strong track record of meaningfully engaging young people.

Legal Registration or Formal Recognition

Applicant organizations must be legally registered or otherwise formally recognized as being permitted to operate in the country from which they are applying.

Proof of this status is one of the documents that must accompany the Expression of Interest.

Relevant Advocacy or Community Engagement Experience

Organizations should demonstrate previous experience in relevant areas or present a credible plan for undertaking the proposed work.

Relevant areas include:

  • Advocacy;
  • Coalition-building;
  • Community engagement;
  • Adolescent health and well-being; and
  • Sexual and reproductive health and rights.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to explain their organizational capacity, proposed activities, and ability to contribute meaningfully to the objectives of the initiative.

Willingness to Collaborate

In countries where national CAAP coalitions and Coordinating Partners already exist, organizations must be willing to work jointly with these existing structures.

Applicants should seek to complement existing work and avoid unnecessary duplication.

This collaborative approach is a significant feature of the 2026–2027 funding phase and reflects the programme’s objective of strengthening national coordination around adolescent health and well-being.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Successful organizations may receive a grant valued at up to US$15,000 per organization.

Applicants should note that US$15,000 represents the stated grant ceiling. Proposed budgets should therefore remain within this limit.

A detailed budget breakdown is required as part of the application.

Organizations should use the budget template provided by PMNCH and ensure that proposed expenditures correspond appropriately with the activities described in their proposal.

Grant Duration

The PMNCH AY Grants 2026–2027 will cover a 12-month implementation period.

The official grant period is:

1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027.

Organizations developing their proposed activities should therefore plan implementation around this timeframe.

How Will Grant Funding Be Disbursed?

Grant funding will not necessarily be provided as one lump-sum payment.

According to the call, funding will be disbursed in instalments tied to agreed deliverables.

Specific arrangements will be established through the grant agreement and Terms of Reference.

Disbursement will also depend on the submission of required reports.

Successful applicants should therefore be prepared to comply with reporting obligations and demonstrate progress against agreed activities and deliverables throughout the grant period.

Required Application Documents

Organizations interested in applying need to submit a complete Expression of Interest package.

Applications must include the following four major components:

1. Proposal

Applicants must submit a proposal using the template provided by PMNCH.

The proposal should describe the key activities the organization intends to implement under the relevant sub-deliverables outlined in the Terms of Reference.

Applicants should carefully review the Terms of Reference before developing their proposal so that proposed activities clearly correspond with the initiative’s objectives and expected deliverables.

2. Budget Breakdown

Organizations must prepare and submit a budget using the template provided by PMNCH.

The proposed budget must remain within the maximum indicative grant ceiling of US$15,000.

The budget should correspond with the activities proposed in the application and provide a clear picture of how the requested funding would support implementation.

3. Proof of Legal Registration or Formal Recognition

Applicants must provide evidence demonstrating that their organization is legally registered or otherwise formally recognized to operate within the country of application.

Organizations should ensure that the documentation submitted clearly establishes their formal status.

4. Brief Organizational Profile

A brief organizational profile must also accompany the application.

This provides applicants with an opportunity to present relevant information about their organization, including its background, work, experience, youth engagement, advocacy capacity, and other characteristics relevant to the proposed initiative.

Application Language

All applications must be submitted in English.

Organizations should therefore ensure that the proposal, budget information, organizational profile, and relevant application materials meet this requirement before submission.

How to Apply for the PMNCH AY Grants 2026–2027

Applications are submitted by email.

Eligible organizations should complete the required proposal and budget templates, assemble the necessary supporting documentation, and submit their complete Expression of Interest to:

Bhavya Nandini
Email: nandinib@who.int

The email must use the following subject-line format:

EOI – Advocating for Change for Adolescents – [Organization Name] – [Country]

Applicants should replace “[Organization Name]” and “[Country]” with their organization’s actual name and country of application.

Before submitting, organizations should ensure that the email contains all four required components:

  1. The completed proposal using the required template;
  2. The completed budget breakdown using the required template;
  3. Proof of legal registration or formal recognition; and
  4. A brief organizational profile.

Applicants should also consult the official Terms of Reference and use the templates supplied by PMNCH rather than creating alternative versions where an official template has been requested.

APPLY NOW

PMNCH AY Grants 2026–2027 Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting an Expression of Interest is:

12:00 CEST on 21 August 2026.

Applications need to be submitted by email no later than this deadline.

Because the deadline includes a specific time and uses Central European Summer Time (CEST), organizations applying from different time zones should carefully convert the deadline into their local time and plan to submit sufficiently early.

Waiting until the final minutes before the deadline may create unnecessary risks associated with internet connectivity, attachments, incorrect documents, or differences in time-zone calculations.

Important Dates to Remember

Applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

  • Expression of Interest deadline: 12:00 CEST, 21 August 2026
  • Grant implementation begins: 1 September 2026
  • Grant implementation ends: 31 August 2027
  • Total grant period: 12 months

The relatively short period between the application deadline and the beginning of the grant period means applicants should ensure that their proposed activities are realistic and that their organizations are prepared to begin implementation promptly if selected.

How Will Applications Be Selected?

Expressions of Interest will be reviewed by the PMNCH Secretariat.

The submission of an application does not automatically mean an organization will receive funding.

Following the initial review, shortlisted organizations may be contacted by PMNCH.

Shortlisted applicants could be invited to participate in a follow-up conversation or asked to provide clarification regarding information contained in their applications before final selections are made.

Organizations should therefore provide accurate and accessible contact information and remain available for potential follow-up communication during the selection process.

Important Conditions Applicants Should Know

Organizations considering this funding opportunity should understand that submitting an Expression of Interest does not guarantee funding.

PMNCH retains discretion over the selection process.

The organization reserves the right to:

  • Accept an application;
  • Reject an application;
  • Request additional information from applicants; or
  • Amend the terms of the call at its discretion.

Applicants should therefore carefully review the official call, Terms of Reference, proposal template, and budget template before making a submission.

Why This Funding Opportunity Matters for Youth-Led Organizations

The PMNCH Advocating for Change for Adolescents Initiative offers more than financial support.

For youth-led organizations and networks working at the national level, the programme provides an opportunity to strengthen advocacy around issues that directly affect adolescents and young people.

The initiative’s emphasis on coordination, capacity-building, government accountability, and national visibility means successful organizations can potentially contribute to broader policy and advocacy processes while strengthening their own organizational and advocacy capacities.

It also recognizes the importance of young people being active participants in decisions concerning adolescent health and well-being.

By supporting youth-led and youth-serving organizations, PMNCH aims to strengthen a generation of advocates capable of engaging governments, civil society, international organizations, philanthropies, and other national stakeholders.

The focus on government commitments is particularly significant because the initiative seeks to connect advocacy with accountability and implementation.

Tips for Preparing an Expression of Interest

Organizations preparing applications should pay close attention to the stated requirements and ensure their submissions demonstrate clear alignment with the initiative.

Applicants should consider the following before submitting:

  1. Review the Terms of Reference carefully. Proposed activities should respond directly to the sub-deliverables and expectations established by PMNCH.
  2. Demonstrate meaningful youth leadership or engagement. Organizations should clearly explain how young people participate in leadership, governance, decision-making, advocacy, or programme implementation.
  3. Show relevant experience. Where applicable, applicants should highlight credible experience in adolescent health, SRHR, advocacy, coalition-building, or community engagement.
  4. Present realistic activities. Proposed work should be achievable within the 12-month grant period.
  5. Keep the budget within the funding ceiling. The total proposed budget should not exceed the stated maximum of US$15,000.
  6. Connect activities with measurable results. Since grant disbursements will be linked to agreed deliverables and reporting, proposed activities should have clear outputs and achievable outcomes.
  7. Explain collaboration plans. Applicants from countries with existing CAAP structures should demonstrate willingness to coordinate with relevant coalitions and Coordinating Partners.
  8. Check supporting documentation. Proof of registration or formal recognition and the organizational profile should be included alongside the proposal and budget.
  9. Follow the required email subject format. Use “EOI – Advocating for Change for Adolescents – [Organization Name] – [Country]”.
  10. Submit before the deadline. The complete application must reach the specified email address by 12:00 CEST on 21 August 2026.

Conclusion

The PMNCH Advocating for Change for Adolescents AY Grants 2026–2027 provide an important funding opportunity for eligible youth-led and youth-serving organizations, coalitions, and networks seeking to strengthen adolescent health and well-being advocacy at the national level.

With grants of up to US$15,000 per organization, the programme will support 12 months of activities focused on stronger national coordination, youth advocacy capacity, accountability for government commitments, and increased visibility of adolescent health and well-being priorities, including sexual and reproductive health and rights.

item.content:encoded:
The DSI/NRF South African Research Chairs Initiative (SARChI) in Transformative Innovation, the 4IR and Sustainable Development at the University of Johannesburg is inviting applications for ten short-term research positions for researchers interested in contributing to a focused research assignment examining innovation agencies in Africa.

The opportunity is designed for PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers and experienced researchers who possess the academic background, research capabilities and analytical skills required to contribute to an intensive research project.

Successful applicants will be appointed for a four-month research assignment and will support the development of focused literature reviews, policy reviews and analytical work examining themes relevant to the role of innovation agencies in supporting economic and societal transformation across Africa.

Applications must be submitted by 21 August 2026.

About the DSI/NRF SARChI Research Opportunity at the University of Johannesburg

The opportunity is offered through the DSI/NRF SARChI in Transformative Innovation, the 4IR and Sustainable Development, based at the University of Johannesburg.

The research initiative is seeking ten researchers to undertake a short-term assignment focused on developing knowledge and analysis around innovation agencies in Africa.

Innovation agencies can play an important role in supporting technological advancement, innovation systems, economic development and broader societal transformation. Understanding how these institutions operate, the policies that influence them, and the ways innovation is financed, governed and evaluated is therefore important for understanding Africa’s evolving innovation landscape.

Researchers selected for this project will contribute to a focused body of research exploring these issues from several complementary perspectives.

Rather than concentrating on only one aspect of innovation, the project identifies multiple research themes spanning innovation policy, green transitions, digital transformation, financing, evaluation and institutional experimentation.

Research Focus: Innovation Agencies in Africa

The central focus of the short-term research assignment is the role of innovation agencies in supporting economic and societal transformation in Africa.

Researchers will be expected to undertake focused literature and policy reviews, identify relevant evidence and debates, synthesise existing knowledge, and prepare written contributions that can feed into the project’s publications and other research outputs.

The advertised areas of interest include, but are not limited to, the following themes.

1. Innovation and Green Transitions

One area of research concerns the relationship between innovation and green transitions.

This theme can involve examining how innovation systems, institutions and policies contribute to transitions towards more sustainable economic and development models.

Researchers positioned within this theme may therefore engage with academic and policy literature concerning innovation, sustainability, institutional change and the role of innovation agencies in facilitating or supporting green economic transformation.

2. Digital Transformation

The project is also interested in digital transformation.

Digital technologies continue to reshape economies, institutions, industries and societies. Within the context of innovation agencies, researchers may examine relevant literature and policy debates surrounding digitalisation and the institutions responsible for encouraging or facilitating innovation.

The theme provides an opportunity to explore how innovation agencies fit into the broader process of technological and economic transformation occurring across African economies.

3. Inclusive Innovation

Another identified research area is inclusive innovation.

Innovation does not automatically generate equally distributed economic or social benefits. Inclusive innovation therefore represents an important area of research when examining how innovation policies and institutions can contribute to broader societal development.

Researchers working in this area will contribute to understanding the relationship between innovation, inclusion and economic or societal transformation within African contexts.

4. Innovation in Policy and Policy Experimentation

The project also identifies innovation in policy and policy experimentation as an area of interest.

This theme recognises that innovation is not limited to technologies, products or businesses. Governments and public institutions can also experiment with new policy approaches, institutional arrangements and mechanisms for supporting innovation.

Research within this theme may examine relevant debates and evidence concerning policy experimentation and innovative approaches to governance and policymaking.

5. Innovation Indicators and Measurement

Another research area concerns innovation indicators and measurement.

Measuring innovation is essential for governments, researchers, policymakers and development institutions seeking to understand whether innovation systems and interventions are producing meaningful outcomes.

Researchers working within this theme may examine approaches used to measure innovation, the indicators applied to innovation systems and the challenges associated with evaluating innovation activity and outcomes.

6. The Evolving Role of Innovation Agencies and Innovation Policy in Africa

The project is particularly concerned with the evolving role of innovation agencies and innovation policy in Africa.

Innovation agencies can occupy an important position between governments, researchers, businesses, entrepreneurs and other actors within innovation ecosystems.

Understanding how their roles are changing is consequently an important component of understanding the broader development of African innovation systems.

Researchers contributing to this theme may examine existing evidence and policy debates surrounding innovation agencies, their mandates, institutional structures and changing roles within African economies.

7. Innovation Financing

Innovation financing is another important area included in the research assignment.

Access to financing can significantly affect the development, adoption and scaling of innovative ideas and technologies. The mechanisms through which innovation is financed can consequently influence the effectiveness of innovation systems.

Researchers focusing on this theme will contribute to the broader examination of how financing relates to innovation agencies and innovation policy.

What Will Selected Researchers Be Expected to Do?

The successful researchers will undertake an intensive research assignment rather than simply participating in general discussions about innovation.

According to the opportunity announcement, researchers will be expected to conduct focused literature and policy reviews.

This means successful applicants should be prepared to identify, review and synthesise relevant academic literature, policy documents, evidence and debates relating to their allocated research theme.

Researchers will also be expected to contribute written material to the project’s publications and other research outputs.

Key responsibilities will therefore include:

  • Conducting focused reviews of relevant academic literature;
  • Reviewing policies and policy-related evidence connected with the assigned research theme;
  • Identifying and synthesising relevant evidence and debates;
  • Undertaking analytical research related to innovation agencies and their contribution to economic and societal transformation;
  • Producing clear, academically rigorous written work;
  • Contributing written inputs to project publications;
  • Contributing to other relevant research outputs;
  • Working independently while meeting the agreed project requirements; and
  • Completing assigned research deliverables within the project’s established timelines.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity is particularly relevant to individuals with postgraduate research experience and a strong interest in innovation, technology, development and public policy.

The University of Johannesburg’s announcement specifically indicates that the research opportunity is seeking PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers and experienced researchers.

Applicants should have relevant postgraduate qualifications and research experience.

Because the appointment is deliverable-based and lasts only four months, candidates should also be comfortable undertaking focused research within defined timelines.

Academic and Research Requirements

Applicants are expected to demonstrate a combination of relevant qualifications, research capabilities and subject knowledge.

Relevant Postgraduate Qualifications and Research Experience

Candidates should possess relevant postgraduate qualifications and research experience.

The announcement does not prescribe one specific postgraduate degree or academic discipline. Applicants should therefore consider how their qualifications and previous research experience relate to the research project’s themes.

Strong Academic Research Skills

Applicants should possess strong academic research skills.

This requirement is particularly important because successful researchers will be responsible for undertaking focused literature and policy reviews and synthesising relevant research evidence.

Strong Analytical Skills

The opportunity requires candidates who can critically analyse information rather than merely collect it.

Applicants should be capable of identifying important themes, arguments, evidence and debates within academic and policy literature and transforming that information into coherent research outputs.

Strong Writing Skills

Strong academic and professional writing abilities are also required.

Successful applicants will contribute written material to project publications and other research outputs. Candidates should therefore be capable of communicating complex research findings clearly, accurately and persuasively.

Relevant Areas of Knowledge

Applicants should demonstrate familiarity with one or more areas connected with the research project.

The announcement specifically identifies familiarity with:

  • Innovation studies;
  • Science, technology and innovation policy;
  • Development studies; and
  • Related fields.

Candidates whose postgraduate studies or professional research experience fall within closely related disciplines may therefore also be relevant, provided they can demonstrate a strong connection between their expertise and the project’s research themes.

Ability to Work Independently

Successful researchers must be able to work independently.

This is especially significant because the positions are short-term and deliverable-based. Researchers will need to manage their assigned work, undertake the necessary reviews and analysis, and produce high-quality outputs within the agreed schedule.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable taking responsibility for their individual research tasks while contributing to the objectives of a wider research project.

Importance of Meeting Agreed Timelines

The researchers must also be able to meet agreed timelines.

The entire appointment lasts four months, meaning the research will take place within a relatively concentrated period.

Candidates should carefully consider their availability before applying and ensure that they can commit sufficient time to completing the required research and written deliverables.

Number of Research Positions Available

A total of ten researchers are being sought for the project.

The availability of multiple positions reflects the breadth of the research agenda, which covers several interconnected themes related to innovation agencies, innovation policy and transformation in Africa.

Applicants should clearly identify the area or theme in which they believe their academic background and research expertise would provide the strongest contribution.

Duration of the Research Appointment

The advertised research positions have a duration of:

Four months

This is therefore a short-term research appointment designed around specific research deliverables rather than a permanent academic position.

Candidates should take the limited duration into consideration when preparing their applications.

Contract Type

The appointment will be structured as a:

Short-term, deliverable-based appointment.

A deliverable-based arrangement means successful researchers will be expected to produce specific research outputs within the agreed project period.

Applicants should consequently be confident in their ability to organise independent research and deliver high-quality written work according to established deadlines.

Remuneration

Successful researchers will receive remuneration in accordance with applicable University of Johannesburg rates.

The announcement does not specify a fixed salary, stipend or total payment amount.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming a particular remuneration figure. Further information concerning applicable rates and payment arrangements may be communicated by the University of Johannesburg as part of the appointment process.

How to Apply for the University of Johannesburg Short-Term Research Positions

The application process requires candidates to prepare and submit two main documents:

  1. A Curriculum Vitae (CV); and
  2. A short motivation letter.

Both documents are important because they will help demonstrate the applicant’s qualifications, research experience and suitability for the project’s research themes.

What to Include in the Motivation Letter

Applicants should pay particular attention to the motivation letter.

The announcement asks applicants to submit a short motivation letter that clearly describes their areas of expertise and identifies the theme or themes on which they would be well positioned to undertake a focused thematic review.

The motivation letter should therefore clearly establish the connection between the applicant’s experience and the research project.

Applicants should consider addressing:

  • Their principal areas of academic or professional research expertise;
  • Their relevant postgraduate research background;
  • Experience with academic literature reviews or policy reviews;
  • Relevant knowledge of innovation studies, science, technology and innovation policy, development studies or related disciplines;
  • The specific research theme or themes that best match their expertise;
  • Why their experience positions them to conduct a focused thematic review;
  • Relevant publications, research projects or policy work, where applicable; and
  • Their ability to undertake independent, high-quality research within the four-month appointment period.

Candidates should avoid submitting an overly generic motivation letter. The advertisement specifically asks applicants to identify the theme or themes on which they would be well positioned to work, making this an important element of the application.

Where to Submit Applications

Applications should be submitted by email to:

UJTRCTISubmissions@uj.ac.za

Applicants should ensure that both their CV and short motivation letter are included before sending the application.

Candidates may also wish to verify that their contact information is current and clearly presented in their CV so that they can be contacted regarding the application if necessary.

Application Deadline: 21 August 2026

The deadline for applications is:

21 August 2026

Prospective applicants should aim to submit their materials before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

Before submitting, applicants should carefully review their CV and motivation letter to ensure that their research expertise and preferred thematic area are clearly explained.

Key Details at a Glance

  • Institution: University of Johannesburg
  • Research initiative: DSI/NRF SARChI in Transformative Innovation, the 4IR and Sustainable Development
  • Research project: Innovation Agencies in Africa
  • Number of researchers sought: 10
  • Duration: Four months
  • Contract: Short-term, deliverable-based appointment
  • Remuneration: In accordance with applicable University of Johannesburg rates
  • Required application documents: CV and short motivation letter
  • Application email: UJTRCTISubmissions@uj.ac.za
  • Application deadline: 21 August 2026

Why This Research Opportunity Is Significant

This short-term research opportunity provides researchers with the chance to contribute to an important area of scholarship and policy analysis concerning Africa’s innovation landscape.

The research themes span some of the most important contemporary issues affecting innovation systems, including digital transformation, green transitions, inclusion, innovation financing, policy experimentation and the measurement of innovation.

The project’s emphasis on innovation agencies is particularly important because these institutions can help connect public policy objectives with research, technological development, entrepreneurship, financing and broader economic transformation.

For PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers and experienced researchers whose expertise aligns with these themes, the assignment provides an opportunity to apply their research capabilities to a focused project addressing innovation and transformation in an African context.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants should ensure that their submissions respond directly to the requirements contained in the announcement.

A strong application should demonstrate clear alignment between the candidate’s expertise and at least one of the project’s identified themes.

Before submitting, candidates should:

  1. Update their CV to highlight postgraduate qualifications, research experience, publications and relevant policy or academic work.
  2. Identify their strongest research theme or themes from the areas listed in the announcement.
  3. Tailor the motivation letter to explain precisely how their expertise relates to those themes.
  4. Highlight research and analytical capabilities, particularly experience conducting literature reviews, policy reviews or related academic research.
  5. Demonstrate strong writing experience by highlighting publications, reports, policy papers, dissertations, theses or other substantial research outputs where relevant.
  6. Show evidence of independent research experience, since successful applicants must be able to work independently.
  7. Confirm availability for the four-month appointment, taking into account the deliverable-based nature of the research.
  8. Review all application documents carefully before emailing them to the specified submission address.

Important Information for Applicants

Applicants should rely on the official opportunity announcement when preparing their submissions.

The advertisement specifies the broad research themes, qualifications, application documents, duration, remuneration arrangement, submission email and deadline. However, it does not provide detailed information about matters such as the exact remuneration amount, individual deliverables for each researcher, work location requirements or a detailed selection timetable.

Applicants should therefore avoid making assumptions about conditions that have not been specified in the announcement.

Conclusion

The University of Johannesburg DSI/NRF SARChI short-term research positions for the Innovation Agencies in Africa project present a valuable opportunity for PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers and experienced researchers with expertise related to innovation, science and technology policy, development studies and associated disciplines.

With ten research positions available, the project will bring together researchers to undertake focused literature and policy reviews examining how innovation agencies can contribute to economic and societal transformation across Africa.

The research encompasses a wide range of important themes, including innovation and green transitions, digital transformation, inclusive innovation, policy experimentation, innovation indicators and measurement, innovation financing, and the evolving role of innovation agencies and innovation policy in Africa.

Successful researchers will be appointed for four months under a short-term, deliverable-based arrangement and will receive remuneration according to applicable University of Johannesburg rates.

Interested applicants must prepare a CV and short motivation letter clearly explaining their areas of expertise and identifying the research theme or themes for which they are best positioned to undertake a focused thematic review.

Applications should be emailed to UJTRCTISubmissions@uj.ac.za no later than 21 August 2026.

Researchers who meet the requirements and whose expertise aligns with the project’s themes should prepare their applications promptly and ensure that their submissions clearly demonstrate the relevance of their qualifications, research experience and thematic expertise.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Marburg in Germany is accepting applications for ten Doctoral Researcher/PhD positions within the new DFG Research Training Group 3159, “Gender and Gendering in Contexts of International Criminal Law.”

Hosted by the International Centre for War Crimes Trials (ICWC) at the University of Marburg, the Research Training Group brings together scholars from multiple disciplines to investigate how gender and processes of gendering interact with international criminal law, transitional justice, institutions, societies, and the broader conditions under which international criminal justice operates.

The positions offer selected doctoral researchers the opportunity to complete an independent PhD project in an international, interdisciplinary, and structured research environment while being employed by the University of Marburg.

A total of 10 positions are available.

Successful applicants are expected to begin on 1 February 2027. The positions are offered for up to four years, with contracts running until 31 January 2031, subject to applicable German academic employment regulations.

The positions are 75% part-time appointments and are remunerated according to TV-H pay grade E13 at 75%, the public-sector salary framework used in the German state of Hesse.

Applications must be submitted by 4 October 2026.

About the University of Marburg

The University of Marburg, formally known as Philipps-Universität Marburg, was founded in 1527 and is one of Germany’s historic universities.

Today, the institution serves approximately 22,000 students and conducts research across a broad range of academic disciplines.

The advertised doctoral positions are based within the University’s International Centre for War Crimes Trials, an interdisciplinary institution focusing on international criminal law, transitional justice, accountability, war crimes, and related political, historical, legal, and societal questions.

The doctoral researchers will form part of DFG Research Training Group 3159, creating a structured environment in which PhD candidates can develop individual dissertation projects while participating in a wider collaborative research programme.

About DFG Research Training Group 3159

The Research Training Group is titled:

Gender and Gendering in Contexts of International Criminal Law

Its central research focus concerns the complex relationships between concepts of gender and international criminal law.

Rather than examining international criminal law exclusively as a technical legal system, the programme investigates the wider legal, political, institutional, cultural, social, and historical contexts in which international criminal justice operates.

The Research Training Group asks how:

  • Gender shapes international criminal law;
  • Processes of gendering influence international criminal justice;
  • International criminal law itself constructs or reproduces ideas about gender;
  • Gender influences institutions responsible for criminal accountability;
  • Gender affects how crimes are understood, categorized, prosecuted, or remembered;
  • International criminal law interacts with social and political structures;
  • Gender shapes the application, function, and impact of international criminal justice.

The programme is intentionally interdisciplinary.

This means doctoral candidates are not restricted to legal research. Applicants from social sciences, humanities, law, economics, theology, and related fields are encouraged to develop projects that contribute to the Research Training Group’s overarching questions.

Number of PhD Positions Available

The University of Marburg is recruiting:

10 Doctoral Researchers/PhD candidates

for the Research Training Group.

This cohort-based structure gives selected doctoral researchers the opportunity to develop their own dissertations alongside other researchers working on connected questions.

The programme therefore combines:

  • Independent doctoral research;
  • Structured supervision;
  • Interdisciplinary exchange;
  • Collaborative research;
  • International academic engagement;
  • Professional development.

Starting Date

The positions are scheduled to begin on:

1 February 2027

Applicants should therefore be available to commence their doctoral employment and research programme around this date.

Contract Duration

The positions are offered until:

31 January 2031

This corresponds to a maximum period of approximately four years.

However, the announcement notes that previous periods of academic qualification employment may need to be taken into consideration under German academic employment law.

The employment limitation is governed by Section 2(1) of the German Academic Fixed-Term Contract Act, commonly known as the Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz or WissZeitVG.

The contract period is intended to provide sufficient time for candidates to undertake the scientific research necessary to complete their doctoral qualifications.

Salary and Employment Conditions

Successful candidates will be employed under the public-sector salary framework of the German state of Hesse.

The position is classified as:

TV-H E13, 75%

The employment volume is therefore:

75% of regular working hours

Applicants should understand that this is a salaried doctoral researcher position, rather than a conventional scholarship that simply provides a stipend.

Candidates will be employees of the University and will combine doctoral research with responsibilities associated with the Research Training Group.

Main Responsibilities

The doctoral researchers will have three principal responsibilities.

1. Complete a Doctoral Degree

The primary purpose of the position is to undertake an independent doctoral research project.

The dissertation topic must fall within the broader research programme of RTG 3159.

Applicants are therefore expected to develop an original research question that connects meaningfully with themes concerning:

  • Gender;
  • Gendering;
  • International criminal law;
  • Transitional justice;
  • International criminal justice;
  • Related institutional, legal, political, historical, economic, cultural, religious, or societal questions.

The exact topic will depend on the applicant’s disciplinary background and research interests.

2. Provide Research Assistance within the Research Training Group

Doctoral researchers will also contribute research assistance to the broader research programme of the RTG.

This reflects the collaborative nature of a DFG Research Training Group.

Candidates should therefore be willing to contribute not only to their individual dissertation but also to the intellectual development of the wider programme.

3. Participate Actively in RTG Activities

Successful candidates must actively participate in the Research Training Group’s activities.

Importantly, on-site participation in the RTG’s core programme is mandatory.

Applicants should therefore not regard the positions as remote PhDs.

While individual research may involve travel, fieldwork, archives, conferences, or international collaboration, doctoral researchers are expected to be physically present for the programme’s central academic activities in Marburg.

Academic Background Required

Applicants must hold an above-average completed university degree equivalent to a:

  • Master’s degree;
  • State examination; or
  • Comparable higher university qualification.

The degree should be in a discipline relevant to the Research Training Group.

The announcement particularly identifies the following fields.

Peace and Conflict Studies

Candidates from peace and conflict studies may develop projects examining areas such as:

  • Transitional justice;
  • Conflict-related violence;
  • Post-conflict accountability;
  • Gender and peacebuilding;
  • International criminal justice;
  • Conflict transformation.

Gender Studies

Gender studies is directly relevant to the programme’s core intellectual agenda.

Potential research could engage with questions involving:

  • Gender theory;
  • Feminist theory;
  • Masculinities;
  • Queer theory;
  • Intersectionality;
  • Gendered institutions;
  • Gendered forms of violence;
  • Gender and justice.

History

Historians may approach international criminal justice and gender from historical perspectives.

Possible research areas could include the development of international criminal institutions, historical war-crimes trials, changing legal concepts, memory, or gendered understandings of conflict and accountability.

Modern German Literature

The programme also explicitly welcomes relevant applicants from modern German literary studies.

Potential projects may engage with representation, discourse, memory, law, gender, violence, testimony, or cultural responses to international crimes.

Political Science

Political scientists may investigate topics related to:

  • International institutions;
  • Global governance;
  • Transitional justice;
  • Conflict;
  • Gender politics;
  • International organizations;
  • Accountability;
  • International criminal courts;
  • Politics of prosecution.

Law

Applicants from law may be particularly well placed to examine doctrinal and theoretical questions surrounding:

  • International criminal law;
  • International humanitarian law;
  • Human rights law;
  • Gender-based crimes;
  • Sexual violence;
  • International tribunals;
  • Transitional justice.

Sociology

Sociological projects may explore how international criminal justice interacts with:

  • Social structures;
  • Institutions;
  • Communities;
  • Gender norms;
  • Identities;
  • Power relations;
  • Collective memory;
  • Social change.

Theology

Theology is also identified as a relevant discipline, reflecting the programme’s broad interdisciplinary approach.

Possible areas might include religion, gender, conflict, reconciliation, ethics, justice, memory, or post-conflict societies.

Economics

Applicants with an economics background may also be eligible where their proposed project connects convincingly with the RTG’s research agenda.

The list of disciplines is introduced as particularly relevant rather than necessarily exhaustive. Applicants from related fields should therefore assess whether their academic training and proposed project fit the Research Training Group’s central research questions.

Previous Research Knowledge

Prior knowledge of the Research Training Group’s main subject areas is considered advantageous.

Relevant background may include experience with:

  • International law;
  • International criminal law;
  • Transitional justice;
  • Gender studies.

This knowledge is described as an advantage rather than an absolute standalone eligibility requirement.

Applicants from adjacent disciplines may therefore still be competitive if they can demonstrate a convincing intellectual connection between their existing background and their proposed doctoral research.

English Language Requirement

Applicants must demonstrate English proficiency of at least:

C1 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages

Proof of English-language proficiency must be included in the application.

Because the programme is international and interdisciplinary, candidates should be capable of:

  • Academic reading;
  • Academic writing;
  • Research presentations;
  • Seminar participation;
  • Interdisciplinary discussion;
  • Professional communication

at an advanced level in English.

Is German Required?

German-language proficiency is not presented as an absolute prerequisite.

However, German skills are considered an advantage.

Candidates who do not currently speak German should demonstrate a:

Willingness to learn German.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to international applicants who already possess strong English-language skills but may not yet have advanced German proficiency.

Personal and Professional Qualities

In addition to academic qualifications, candidates should demonstrate:

  • Team spirit;
  • Strong commitment to academic excellence;
  • Interest in interdisciplinary research;
  • Willingness to collaborate;
  • Capacity for independent scientific research;
  • Commitment to completing a doctoral qualification.

The programme is designed for researchers who can work independently while contributing actively to a collaborative academic community.

Interdisciplinary Research Is Central

One of the most important characteristics of RTG 3159 is its interdisciplinary structure.

Applicants should therefore avoid developing a dissertation proposal that is intellectually isolated from the wider programme.

The proposed research should be suitable for dialogue with scholars from other disciplines.

For example, a legal research project may benefit from considering:

  • Political institutions;
  • Historical developments;
  • Gender theory;
  • Social structures;
  • Cultural narratives.

Similarly, a sociology, political science, history, or gender-studies project should demonstrate a meaningful relationship with international criminal law or the broader systems surrounding it.

Structured Doctoral Supervision

Successful candidates will receive structured doctoral supervision.

Each doctoral researcher will have an individually composed:

Thesis Advisory Committee

This committee is intended to provide structured guidance throughout the doctoral project.

Such supervision can help candidates with:

  • Research design;
  • Dissertation planning;
  • Academic development;
  • Research challenges;
  • Publication strategies;
  • Career planning;
  • Interdisciplinary integration.

Individual Qualification and Supervision Programme

The Research Training Group will provide an individual qualification programme tailored to both:

  • The doctoral researcher; and
  • The individual dissertation project.

This provides an opportunity for candidates to develop not only their thesis but also a broader academic research profile.

International and Interdisciplinary Research Environment

The University emphasizes that the successful doctoral researchers will join an:

  • Inspiring;
  • International;
  • Interdisciplinary

academic environment.

A major objective of the programme is to enable doctoral candidates to build their own independent research profiles.

This can be particularly useful for candidates considering longer-term careers in:

  • Academia;
  • International organizations;
  • Transitional justice;
  • Human rights;
  • Policy research;
  • International criminal justice;
  • NGOs;
  • Research institutes;
  • Legal institutions.

Additional University Support

Doctoral researchers will also have access to support and professional-development structures within the University of Marburg.

These include support from:

Marburg University Research Academy

The Research Academy provides doctoral and early-career researchers with training and professional-development opportunities.

International Office

International doctoral researchers can receive institutional support related to international mobility and integration.

Family Service

The University describes itself as family-friendly and provides services intended to help employees balance professional and family responsibilities.

Higher Education Didactics

Candidates can also access university services related to higher education teaching and pedagogical development.

Research Environment and Inclusion

The University describes the research environment as:

  • Collegial;
  • Family-friendly;
  • LGBTIQ+-inclusive.

The University also explicitly encourages applications from women.

In areas where women are underrepresented, female candidates may be preferred when applicants have equal qualifications.

Applicants with disabilities, as defined under the relevant provisions of Germany’s Social Security Code, may also receive preference in cases of equal qualifications.

Application Documents

Applications may be submitted in:

German or English

Candidates must prepare several substantial documents.

1. Doctoral Project Outline

Applicants must submit an outline of their planned doctoral research project.

Maximum length:

10 pages

The page limit includes:

  • Research proposal;
  • Work schedule;
  • Time schedule;
  • Bibliography.

The proposal must be based on an:

Innovative research question

that aligns with the topic and research programme of RTG 3159.

The project should also be suitable for interdisciplinary collaboration.

This is likely to be one of the most important components of the application.

What Should the Doctoral Proposal Demonstrate?

Although the announcement does not prescribe a detailed proposal template, the research outline should clearly demonstrate:

  • The proposed research problem;
  • Central research question;
  • Relevance to gender and gendering;
  • Connection with international criminal law;
  • Original academic contribution;
  • Theoretical framework;
  • Methodological approach;
  • Interdisciplinary relevance;
  • Feasibility within the four-year period;
  • Planned research stages.

Candidates should ensure that their proposal connects explicitly to the Research Training Group rather than simply submitting a generic PhD proposal.

2. Writing Sample

Applicants must submit a writing sample of no more than:

25 pages

Possible writing samples include:

  • Sections from a Master’s thesis;
  • Table of contents and selected Master’s thesis chapters;
  • Seminar paper;
  • Research paper;
  • Academic article;
  • Blog entry.

The writing sample allows the selection committee to assess the applicant’s research, analytical, and writing abilities.

Candidates should ideally choose work that demonstrates qualities relevant to the proposed PhD.

3. Motivation Letter

Applicants must submit a letter explaining their motivation.

A strong motivation letter should connect:

  • Previous academic background;
  • Research interests;
  • Proposed doctoral project;
  • Interest in RTG 3159;
  • Interest in interdisciplinary research;
  • Career goals.

Rather than simply describing the University as prestigious, applicants should explain why this specific Research Training Group is a strong intellectual fit.

4. Curriculum Vitae

A current CV is required.

Candidates should include relevant:

  • Academic qualifications;
  • Research experience;
  • Employment;
  • Publications;
  • Conference participation;
  • Research projects;
  • Teaching;
  • Academic service;
  • Language abilities;
  • Awards.

5. Certificates of Qualification

Applicants must submit certificates documenting their completed qualifications.

This includes evidence of the university degree that qualifies them for doctoral research.

6. Evidence of Academic Activities

Where applicable, candidates should include documentation of relevant academic activities.

These might include research, publications, conference contributions, academic employment, or other scholarly work.

7. Transcript of Records

A complete academic transcript must be submitted.

The transcript should document courses and academic performance from the applicant’s relevant degree programme.

8. Proof of English Proficiency

Applicants must provide evidence demonstrating English proficiency at:

C1 level or higher

Candidates should review the application system carefully to determine which forms of certification are accepted.

9. Academic Recommendation or Master’s Thesis Evaluation

Applicants must provide one of the following:

  • One academic letter of recommendation, OR
  • The first examiner’s report/evaluation of the Master’s thesis

This flexibility is important for candidates who may find it easier to provide an official Master’s thesis examiner report than request a separate reference.

Application Checklist

Before submitting, applicants should ensure they have:

  1. Doctoral project outline, maximum 10 pages;
  2. Work and time schedule included in the proposal;
  3. Bibliography included within the 10-page limit;
  4. Writing sample, maximum 25 pages;
  5. Motivation letter;
  6. CV;
  7. Qualification certificates;
  8. Evidence of academic activities where applicable;
  9. Transcript of records;
  10. Proof of English C1 proficiency;
  11. One academic recommendation OR first examiner’s Master’s thesis report.

Selection Interviews

Digital interviews are expected to take place from:

Late October to early November 2026

Applicants shortlisted after the document review should therefore monitor their email closely during this period and be prepared for an online interview.

Candidates may reasonably expect the interview to explore their proposed research, disciplinary background, motivation, interdisciplinary fit, and suitability for the Research Training Group.

Application Deadline

The final deadline is:

4 October 2026

Applicants should submit their complete application by this date.

Given that the research proposal alone can be up to 10 pages and requires an innovative project aligned with the RTG research programme, prospective candidates should begin preparing significantly before October.

Important Dates

Applications: Open

Application deadline: 4 October 2026

Expected interviews: Late October to early November 2026

Employment and PhD start: 1 February 2027

Contract end: 31 January 2031

Maximum duration: Approximately four years

Registration Number

Applicants should note the official vacancy registration number:

ZE-0063-ICWC-wmz-2026

This reference may be useful when communicating with the University about the vacancy.

Contact for Further Information

Questions concerning the doctoral positions or Research Training Group may be directed to:

Prof. Dr. Stefanie Bock

Telephone: +49 6421-28 23119

Email:

rtg3159@uni-marburg.de

Further information about the Research Training Group is available HERE.

 

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

Start With the Research Training Group, Not Just Your Existing Interests

Read the RTG research programme carefully before finalizing your proposal.

A strong application should demonstrate that the candidate understands what the programme is trying to investigate.

Make Gender Central to the Research Question

The programme is specifically concerned with gender and gendering.

Gender should therefore be analytically important to the project rather than appearing only as a secondary variable added to an otherwise unrelated proposal.

Establish a Strong Connection to International Criminal Law

Applicants from non-law disciplines should explain clearly how their project interacts with international criminal justice.

This connection could be:

  • Institutional;
  • Political;
  • Historical;
  • Sociological;
  • Cultural;
  • Economic;
  • Religious;
  • Legal.

Demonstrate Interdisciplinary Potential

The application should show how the project could benefit from conversations with researchers outside the applicant’s own field.

Develop a Realistic Four-Year Timeline

Candidates should show that the proposed research can reasonably be completed within the employment period.

The time plan should account for major stages such as:

  • Literature review;
  • Theoretical development;
  • Data gathering where applicable;
  • Archival or field research;
  • Analysis;
  • Chapter writing;
  • Revision;
  • Dissertation submission.

Choose Your Writing Sample Carefully

The strongest writing sample is not necessarily the longest or most prestigious piece.

Choose work that best demonstrates:

  • Independent thinking;
  • Clear argumentation;
  • Research ability;
  • Methodological competence;
  • Academic writing.

Explain Why Marburg and RTG 3159

Your motivation letter should make clear why this programme provides a particularly strong environment for your project.

Specificity is more persuasive than generic praise.

Conclusion

The 10 Doctoral Researcher/PhD positions at the University of Marburg’s DFG Research Training Group 3159 offer a substantial opportunity for emerging researchers interested in the intersections of gender, gendering, international criminal law, transitional justice, conflict, institutions, society, and accountability.

Successful applicants will join an international and interdisciplinary doctoral cohort at the International Centre for War Crimes Trials and receive structured supervision through an individually composed Thesis Advisory Committee.

The appointments run for up to four years, beginning 1 February 2027 and ending 31 January 2031, and are paid according to TV-H E13 at 75% employment.

The programme welcomes applicants from a broad range of relevant disciplines, including peace and conflict studies, gender studies, history, modern German literature, political science, law, sociology, theology, and economics.

Applicants need an above-average relevant university degree, at least C1-level English, a strong research profile, and an original doctoral project aligned with the RTG’s interdisciplinary research agenda. German is advantageous but applicants who are willing to learn German may also be considered.

The application requires a substantial doctoral proposal, writing sample, motivation letter, academic records, proof of English proficiency, and either an academic recommendation or the first examiner’s report on the applicant’s Master’s thesis.

The application deadline is 4 October 2026, with online selection interviews expected from late October through early November.

For researchers seeking a salaried PhD position combining international criminal justice with gender-focused interdisciplinary research, this opportunity provides a particularly structured pathway to developing an independent academic profile in Germany.

For further information about this opportunity, VISIT HERE.

For more doctoral, research, and international opportunities, visit www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.
