item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for two major Melton Foundation opportunities for 2027: the Global Solvers Accelerator and the Global Citizenship Learning Program. Both programs are designed to develop globally minded leaders, strengthen community impact and connect emerging changemakers with an international network committed to sustainable development and global citizenship.

Although both opportunities provide pathways into the Melton Foundation’s lifelong global community, they serve different applicants. The Global Solvers Accelerator is intended for young social-impact practitioners who are already leading or actively involved in a community project. The Global Citizenship Learning Program is designed specifically for university students enrolled at one of the Melton Foundation’s five partner institutions.

Applications for both 2027 cohorts opened on 15 August 2026 and will close on 15 November 2026. Prospective applicants should carefully compare the eligibility requirements before selecting the most appropriate program.

Melton Foundation 2027 Programs at a Glance

Detail Global Solvers Accelerator Global Citizenship Learning Program
Target participants Young social-impact and community-development practitioners University students interested in community impact and global citizenship
Age requirement 20–35 years 18–25 years
Geographic scope Open to eligible applicants worldwide Restricted to students at five partner universities
Existing project required Yes No established track record is required
Main format Virtual learning with a fully funded in-person Co-Lab Virtual learning with a fully sponsored Global Citizens’ Connect
Learning period Eight-month core program, supported by onboarding and transition activities Ten-month program from March to December 2027
Weekly commitment Approximately four hours Approximately three to four hours
Program cost USD 900 if selected; partial need-based support is available No program fee
Application deadline 15 November 2026 15 November 2026
Long-term outcome Entry into the Melton Fellowship after successful completion Entry into the Melton Fellowship after successful completion

About the Melton Foundation

The Melton Foundation is an international organization focused on developing people who can collaborate across cultures, identities, sectors and geographic boundaries. Its programs connect local community action with global citizenship and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Rather than offering isolated training events, the Foundation develops sustained learning communities. Participants are expected to contribute actively, learn from people with different experiences and apply their learning to practical social or community challenges.

Successful participants in both programs can eventually join the Melton Fellowship, a lifelong international community offering continued opportunities for mentoring, collaboration, leadership development, learning and social-impact partnerships.

Opportunity One: Global Solvers Accelerator 2027

What Is the Global Solvers Accelerator?

The Global Solvers Accelerator is a leadership, project-development and peer-learning program for emerging changemakers between 20 and 35 years of age.

It brings together approximately 15 to 20 practitioners from different countries who are already working on community-based or social-impact initiatives. Participants use the program to examine their leadership practices, address unresolved project challenges, learn from international peers and improve the effectiveness and sustainability of their initiatives.

The Accelerator is not simply a business-growth program. Its emphasis is on reflective leadership, shared learning, collaborative problem-solving and the development of stronger social-impact projects. Participants bring actual problems, decisions and operational challenges from their initiatives into a structured international learning environment.

Previous participants have worked in areas including:

  • Education and learning equity
  • Climate action and environmental sustainability
  • Public health
  • Civic engagement
  • Community livelihoods
  • Disability inclusion
  • Human rights
  • Social equity
  • Youth empowerment
  • Technology for social good
  • Other areas connected with sustainable development

Global Solvers Accelerator Learning Structure

The core Accelerator runs from 1 April to 30 November 2027 and includes eight interconnected learning modules. Selected participants are expected to complete onboarding activities in March 2027 before entering the main learning phase.

The program combines:

  • Facilitated thematic modules
  • Bi-weekly virtual sessions
  • Independent assignments and preparation
  • Peer-to-peer learning
  • Project-based exercises
  • Practical social-impact tools
  • Subject-matter advice
  • Mentoring and personalized support
  • Cross-cultural dialogue
  • Collaborative problem-solving
  • Reflection on leadership, systems and project strategy

According to the official GSA frequently asked questions, learning topics may include project effectiveness, team dynamics, collective leadership, intersectionality, social innovation, regenerative practices, impact modelling, systems-based approaches, strategic visibility, audience engagement, and monitoring and evaluation.

Participants also map their projects against the Sustainable Development Goals. The purpose is not to limit projects to selected SDGs, but to help participants understand how their local initiatives connect with the wider, interconnected sustainable-development agenda.

Levels of Impact

The Accelerator is designed to produce change at three interconnected levels:

  1. Individual development

Participants strengthen their leadership capacity, intercultural understanding, critical reflection and ability to work across differences.

  1. Community-level impact

Participants apply new methods, ideas and relationships to strengthen the projects they are implementing in their respective communities.

  1. Wider systemic impact

By exchanging locally grounded knowledge across countries and sectors, participants can identify common challenges, adapt successful approaches and contribute to wider progress toward sustainable development.

Who Should Apply?

The Global Solvers Accelerator is suitable for applicants who:

  • Are between 20 and 35 years old.
  • Are actively involved in or leading a community or social-impact project.
  • Can demonstrate a genuine commitment to creating positive change.
  • Are interested in improving their leadership and project practices.
  • Are willing to learn through peer exchange and honest reflection.
  • Can collaborate respectfully with people from different cultures and backgrounds.
  • Have sufficient English-language ability to participate in all program activities.
  • Can commit approximately four hours per week.
  • Can participate in virtual sessions and complete independent assignments.
  • Can maintain at least a 75% participation rate.

An academic degree or a particular field of study is not identified as a mandatory requirement. However, having an existing social-impact project or initiative is essential.

Project Eligibility Requirements

Applicants cannot apply without a project. The initiative may be at an early planning stage or already under implementation, but it must:

  • Already exist as a concrete project or documented project plan.
  • Address a real community or social challenge.
  • Be connected to a particular community, territory or on-the-ground context.
  • Continue for at least the duration of the Accelerator.
  • Provide the applicant with sufficient responsibility or involvement to apply the program’s learning.

Applications are submitted by individuals rather than project teams. If several people are working on one initiative, the group should nominate the member best positioned to represent the project and apply.

Global Solvers Co-Lab 2027

Actively engaged participants will be invited to the Global Solvers Co-Lab, the Accelerator’s fully funded, week-long in-person component.

The 2027 Co-Lab is tentatively scheduled for 19–26 July 2027. It is designed as an intensive working experience where participants meet their peers, examine projects, exchange practical knowledge, develop collaborations and design new approaches to community impact.

Applicants should understand that the Co-Lab is not a sightseeing trip or leisure retreat. Participants should expect structured activities, collaborative workshops, shared learning environments and an intensive schedule.

Benefits of the Global Solvers Accelerator

Selected participants can expect to:

  • Improve their leadership and decision-making capacity.
  • Receive structured support for an existing social-impact project.
  • Learn practical tools for project planning, implementation and evaluation.
  • Strengthen their understanding of systems, communities and sustainable development.
  • Obtain constructive feedback from international peers.
  • Build relationships with social-impact practitioners from different countries.
  • Access mentoring and subject-matter guidance.
  • Develop approaches to project communication and strategic visibility.
  • Participate in a fully funded international Co-Lab, subject to active engagement.
  • Join the Melton Foundation’s lifelong community after successful completion.

The Foundation reports that, among its 2025 Accelerator participants, 94% became more intentional about collaboration and partnerships, while 91% reported a strong sense of trust and belonging within the community.

Program Fee and Financial Support

The program fee for the 2027 Global Solvers Accelerator is USD 900, payable only after an applicant has been selected.

Need-based financial support is available at different levels, covering 20%, 50% or up to 80% of the fee. Full fee support is not currently offered. Applicants receiving the maximum 80% support would remain responsible for 20% of the program fee.

Requesting financial support does not negatively affect the selection decision. However, applicants must request it in their original application. Requests submitted after the application stage cannot be considered.

Applicants seeking financial support must generally prepare:

  • A personal statement explaining their financial circumstances and need for assistance.
  • An endorsement letter from a credible reference, such as a project supervisor or co-leader.

Applicants should consult the official GSA Application Guide for the exact documentation requirements.

Global Solvers Accelerator Application and Selection Timeline

The anticipated process is:

  1. Application period: 15 August–15 November 2026
  2. Application and reference review: December 2026–January 2027
  3. Virtual Assessment Centre: tentatively around 30–31 January 2027
  4. Onboarding: March 2027
  5. Core Accelerator: 1 April–30 November 2027
  6. Global Solvers Co-Lab: tentatively 19–26 July 2027
  7. Transition into the Melton Fellowship: after successful program completion

The official main page and FAQ currently display different tentative Assessment Centre dates—30 and 31 January 2027—so shortlisted applicants should follow the date stated in their invitation.

Applicants may submit the Global Solvers Accelerator 2027 application here.

Opportunity Two: Global Citizenship Learning Program 2027

What Is the Global Citizenship Learning Program?

The Global Citizenship Learning Program is a ten-month learning and leadership experience for university students who want to understand global challenges, collaborate across cultures and create positive change in their communities.

The program runs online from March to December 2027 and combines eight learning modules with onboarding, practical assignments, intercultural dialogue, community-impact work and a transition into the lifelong Melton Fellowship.

Unlike the Global Solvers Accelerator, applicants are not required to have an established social-impact initiative or an extensive record of leadership. The selection process places considerable emphasis on motivation, potential, curiosity and commitment to community impact.

What Participants Will Learn

Participants develop practical and interpersonal competencies such as:

  • Intercultural awareness and communication
  • Critical thinking
  • Empathy and active listening
  • Inclusive and ethical leadership
  • Project management
  • Systems thinking
  • Storytelling
  • Collaborative problem-solving
  • Teamwork across cultures
  • Understanding inequality, privilege and inclusion
  • Connecting global challenges with local realities
  • Sustainable Development Goal implementation

Students work with international peers, Senior Melton Fellows and community partners to co-create projects aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. These are intended to produce real community outcomes rather than remain theoretical classroom exercises.

Program Format and Time Commitment

The program involves approximately three to four hours of participation per week, equivalent to around 12 to 16 hours per month.

A typical month may include:

  • Self-paced learning materials
  • Two live virtual cohort meetings
  • Progress on a community-impact project
  • Campus or local-team meetings
  • Required readings and preparatory activities
  • Group discussions
  • Collaborative assignments
  • Reflection and peer-learning exercises

Live sessions are generally held twice monthly, commonly on the first and third Saturdays. Participants must also have access to a laptop or desktop computer, stable internet, a camera and a microphone.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must:

  • Be between 18 and 25 years old.
  • Be currently enrolled at an eligible partner university.
  • Have an interest in local community impact.
  • Have sufficient English-language skills to follow discussions and communicate with other participants.
  • Be willing to collaborate across cultures, identities and perspectives.
  • Commit approximately three to four hours per week.
  • Participate actively in virtual and in-person activities.
  • Complete required assignments and preparatory work.

Preference is given to students who expect to remain at their university for at least two years after the program begins. This supports continued participation in campus teams and long-term local activities.

Eligible Partner Universities

Only students currently enrolled at the following institutions may apply:

  1. Ashesi University, Accra, Ghana
  2. B.M.S. Group of Institutions, Bangalore, India
  3. Universidad de La Frontera, Temuco, Chile
  4. Friedrich Schiller University, Jena, Germany
  5. Dillard University, New Orleans, United States

Students at other universities are not eligible for this particular program, even if they meet the age requirement. They may instead consider the Global Solvers Accelerator if they are aged 20–35 and have an eligible community initiative.

Global Citizens’ Connect

Actively engaged participants may attend the Global Citizens’ Connect, a fully sponsored, week-long international gathering.

The Foundation states that travel, accommodation and participation costs are covered for eligible, actively engaged participants. The gathering brings the cohort together for workshops, intercultural exchange, community engagement and collaborative work on global challenges.

Participation is not intended as tourism or recreational travel. Fellows should expect intensive learning, unfamiliar environments, shared spaces, local food, collaborative responsibilities and structured activities.

Cost and Financial Coverage

The Global Citizenship Learning Program has no program fee. Virtual learning activities are free, and the costs associated with the Global Citizens’ Connect are covered for participants who remain actively engaged and are invited to attend.

Applicants should nevertheless review final participation terms and travel instructions if selected, particularly regarding passports, visas, local transportation and any personal incidental expenses.

Application Process

Applicants must complete an online form containing questions about their experiences, perspectives, motivations, leadership potential and commitment to community impact.

All answers must:

  • Be written in English.
  • Remain within the specified word limits.
  • Be complete.
  • Be submitted before the deadline.
  • Reflect the applicant’s authentic experiences and voice.

The Foundation permits applicants to use artificial-intelligence tools for limited language polishing, but warns against using them to generate the entire application. Applications that appear wholly AI-generated may be eliminated.

Applicants can use the GCLP 2027 Application Guide to prepare their responses before entering them in the online form.

GCLP Selection Process

The selection process involves several stages:

  1. Submission of the online application.
  2. Initial screening by the relevant partner university.
  3. Local assessment or interview, primarily conducted in English.
  4. Nomination of leading candidates for a Global Virtual Assessment Centre.
  5. Assessment of teamwork, problem-solving, communication and understanding of global challenges.
  6. Final selection by an international selection team.

Approximately 20 students are expected to join the cohort. Shortlisted applicants may be invited to a 120-minute virtual Assessment Centre in late January or early February 2027, with final results expected by the end of February 2027.

Applicants should regularly check their email and spam folders and monitor notices from their university’s Melton Foundation campus team.

GCLP Application Deadline

Applications opened on 15 August 2026 and close on:

15 November 2026 at 11:59 p.m. US Eastern Standard Time

Applicants should account for the time-zone difference and avoid waiting until the final day.

Eligible students may submit the Global Citizenship Learning Program 2027 application here.

Which Melton Foundation Program Should You Choose?

Choose the Global Solvers Accelerator if you:

  • Are between 20 and 35 years old.
  • Can apply from any country.
  • Already have a community or social-impact project.
  • Want to strengthen that project through international peer learning.
  • Can pay the program fee or obtain partial need-based support.

Choose the Global Citizenship Learning Program if you:

  • Are between 18 and 25 years old.
  • Are enrolled at one of the five designated partner universities.
  • Want to build global citizenship and leadership skills.
  • Have strong motivation but may not yet have an established social-impact record.
  • Want to participate in a completely free ten-month learning program.

Application Tips for Both Programs

  1. Select the correct pathway

Do not apply solely because both opportunities lead to the Melton Fellowship. Your age, university status and existing project determine which option is appropriate.

  1. Provide specific evidence

Use concrete examples of community involvement, leadership, challenges, learning and impact. Avoid unsupported claims and generic statements.

  1. Explain your motivation clearly

Show why global citizenship, sustainable development and intercultural collaboration matter to your work or future goals.

  1. Be honest about challenges

The Foundation values reflection and learning potential. Explain what you still need to learn and how the program could help you address real limitations.

  1. Protect your authentic voice

Prepare your responses personally. Any language support should preserve your ideas, experiences and natural writing style.

  1. Prepare early

Application forms are detailed. Draft answers offline, respect the word limits and collect references or financial-support documents before the deadline.

  1. Confirm your availability

Both programs require consistent participation. Consider your academic, employment and project responsibilities before committing.

  1. Submit before the closing day

Technical problems, time-zone confusion or missing documents can make an otherwise strong application ineligible.

Conclusion

The Melton Foundation’s Global Solvers Accelerator and Global Citizenship Learning Program offer two distinct routes for young people seeking to strengthen their leadership, community engagement and contribution to sustainable development.

The Global Solvers Accelerator is the stronger option for young practitioners who are already implementing social-impact initiatives and want to improve their projects through structured learning, international collaboration and mentoring. The Global Citizenship Learning Program is designed for eligible university students who want to develop global citizenship skills, work across cultures and begin building a long-term record of community impact.

Applications for both 2027 programs close on 15 November 2026. Interested candidates should review the official eligibility requirements, prepare authentic applications and submit well before the deadline.
